﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger, toward those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾ ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾.

﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger﴾: that is, this is a declaration of freedom. "Min" is for origin/beginning (ibtida'iyya), connected to an elided element whose estimate is "conveyed" (wasila) ﴿from Allah and His Messenger﴾. It is permissible that ﴿a declaration of freedom﴾ be the subject (mubtada') since it is specified by its qualifier, and the predicate is ﴿toward those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾. It was also read with its accusative form (naṣb), as an imperative of "listen to" (isma'ū barā'atan). The meaning is: Allah and His Messenger are free of the covenant that you made with the polytheists. The declaration of freedom was attributed to Allah and His Messenger, and the covenant to the Muslims, to indicate that it is obligatory upon them to repudiate the covenants of the polytheists toward them, even though these were issued by the permission of Allah the Exalted and by agreement of the Messenger, for the two of them are free of them. The reason is that they had made covenants with the polytheists of the Arabs, and they broke them, except for some people among them, the Banu Damra and the Banu Kinana. So He commanded them to repudiate the covenant with those who had broken it, and gave the polytheists a respite of four months to go wherever they wished. He said: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, namely Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja, and al-Muharram, because it was revealed in Shawwal. It is also said that they are twenty days of Dhu al-Hijja, al-Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten days of Rabi' al-Akhir, because the proclamation took place on the day of sacrifice (yawm an-nahr). This is based on what is reported: when it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, riding al-ʿAdba' (his camel), to recite it to the people of the pilgrimage season (al-mawsim). He had sent Abu Bakr, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, as commander over the pilgrimage season. It was said to him: "If only you had sent it with Abu Bakr." He said: "None shall convey it on my behalf except a man from me." When ʿAli, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, drew near, Abu Bakr heard the noise of the camel and stopped and said: "This is the noise of the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." When he reached him, he said: "Are you a commander or one commanded?" He said: "One commanded." When it was before the Tarwiya, Abu Bakr, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, delivered a sermon and informed them about their rites, and ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, stood on the day of sacrifice at the Jamrat al-ʿAqaba and said: "O people, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you." They said: "With what?" So he recited to them thirty or forty verses, then said: "I have been commanded with four: that no polytheist shall approach the House after this year, that no one shall circumambulate the House naked, that no one shall enter Paradise except a believing soul, and that whoever has a covenant shall have it fulfilled for him until its term."

(And perhaps His saying ﷺ "None shall convey on my behalf except a man from me" is not general, for he ﷺ was sent so that many who were not of his kin would convey on his behalf. Rather, it is specific to covenants, for it is the custom of the Arabs that the covenant of a tribe and its annulment is not handled except by a man from that tribe (p-71). This is indicated by what is in some narrations: "It is not fitting for anyone to convey this except a man from my family.")

﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾: you will not get beyond His reach, even if He gives you respite. ﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾: by killing and capture in this world, and by punishment in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 3–4:

﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people﴾: i.e., a far-reaching announcement (i'lam fa'al), in the sense of if'al (proclamation), like amān (safe-conduct) and ʿaṭāʾ (gift). Its nominative case is like that of barāʾa in both readings. ﴿On the day of the greater Hajj﴾: the day of ʿId (the festival of sacrifice), because in it the Hajj is completed and most of its rites are performed, and because the proclamation was made on it. It is also related that the Prophet (ﷺ) stood on the day of sacrifice at the jamarat during the Farewell Pilgrimage and said, "This is the day of the greater Hajj." It was also said that it is the day of ʿArafah, based on his saying (ﷺ), "Hajj is ʿArafah."

The Hajj was described as "greater" either because the ʿUmrah is called the "lesser Hajj," or because what is meant by the Hajj is the acts that occur on that day, which are greater than the rest of the acts, or because that Hajj gathered Muslims and polytheists together and its festival coincided with the festivals of the People of the Book, or because in it the might of the Muslims and the humiliation of the polytheists became manifest. ﴿That Allah﴾: i.e., that Allah. ﴿is free of obligation to the polytheists﴾: i.e., from their covenants. ﴿And His Messenger﴾: it is conjoined to the pronoun in ﴿is free﴾, or to the position of (inna) and its noun in the reading of one who reads it with a kasra, treating the proclamation as having the status of speech; and it is read in the accusative, conjoined to the noun of inna, or because the waw has the sense of "with," and there is no repetition in it. For His saying ﴿a declaration of disassociation from Allah﴾ is information about the establishment of disassociation, whereas this is information about the obligation to announce it; for this reason He attached it to "the people" and did not restrict it to the covenanted ones.

﴿So if you repent﴾: from disbelief and treachery. ﴿it is better for you﴾: so repentance is good for you. ﴿But if you turn away﴾: from repentance, or you persist in turning away from Islam and fidelity. ﴿then know that you will not escape Allah﴾: you will not outrun Him in pursuit, nor will you cause Him to fail by fleeing, in this world. ﴿And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾: in the Hereafter.

﴿Except those of the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾: this is an exception from "the polytheists," or it is a corrective (istidrak), as though it were said to them, after they were commanded to renounce the covenant with the violators: "But those among them with whom you made a covenant" [are excepted]. ﴿Then they have not failed you in anything﴾: of the conditions of the covenant, and they have not breached it, or they have not killed any of you, and they have never harmed you. ﴿Nor have they supported anyone against you﴾: of your enemies. ﴿So fulfill their covenant to them until their term﴾: until the completion of their term, and do not treat them as violators. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾: this is a reason and an indication that fulfilling their covenant is an aspect of righteousness (taqwa).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 5–6:

﴿Then when the sacred months have passed﴾ (fa-idha insalakha): ended. The basic meaning of insilakh (withdrawal, stripping away) is that a thing comes out of what it was clinging to, like the skin being stripped from a sheep (salkh al-shah). ﴿The sacred months﴾ (al-ashhur al-hurum): those in which the covenant-breakers were permitted to travel freely through the land. It is said that they are Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram. But this view disturbs the composition of the verse and contradicts the consensus (ijma', the scholarly agreement), for it requires that the sanctity of the sacred months remain, since nothing revealed afterwards abrogates it. ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾: the covenant-breakers. ﴿Wherever you find them﴾: whether within the sacred territory or outside it. ﴿And seize them﴾: take them captive. Al-akhidh means the captive. ﴿And besiege them﴾: confine them, or prevent them from reaching the Sacred Mosque. ﴿And lie in wait for them at every ambush﴾: at every passage, so that they do not spread out in the lands. The word is in the accusative as an adverb of place (zarf). ﴿But if they repent﴾: turn from polytheism to faith. ﴿And establish prayer and give zakat﴾: as confirmation of their repentance and faith.

(p-72) ﴿Then let them go their way﴾: leave them and do not molest them in any of that. This contains evidence that the one who abandons prayer or withholds zakat should not be left to go his way. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾: this is a justification for the command, meaning: so let them go, because Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, who has forgiven them what had passed and granted them reward through repentance.

﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection﴾: the one who is to be molested is meant here. ﴿Seeks your protection﴾: asks you for safe conduct and requests your protection.

﴿Then grant him protection﴾: give him security. ﴿Until he hears the words of Allah﴾ and reflects upon them and comprehends the reality of the matter. ﴿Then convey him to his place of safety﴾: the place where he is secure, if he does not become Muslim. The word aḥad (anyone) is in the nominative, governed by a verb implied by what follows it, not as a subject (mubtada'), because inna (indeed) is among the particles that govern verbs. ﴿That﴾: the security or the command. ﴿Because they are a people who do not know﴾: what faith is and what the reality of what you call them to is. Therefore their security is necessary for as long as they listen and reflect.

Therefore their security is necessary for as long as they listen and reflect.

**How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger?** This is an interrogative (*istifham*) in the sense of denial (*inkar*) and improbability (*istib'ad*): it is unlikely that they would keep a covenant and not break it, given the rancor in their hearts. Or it means that it is improbable that Allah and His Messenger would keep a covenant with them while they have broken it.

The predicate (*khabar*) of *yakunu* may be **كَيْفَ** (*kayfa*), placed first because of the interrogative; or **لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ** (*lil-mushrikin*); or **عِنْدَ اللَّهِ** (*'inda Allah*). On the first two, *'inda Allah* is an attribute of *'ahd* (covenant), or an adverbial complement (*zarf*) of it, or of *yakunu*. On the last two, *kayfa* is a circumstantial qualifier (*hal*) of *'ahd*. *Lil-mushrikin*, if it is not the predicate, is an explanatory elaboration (*tabyin*).

**Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram.** These are the ones excepted earlier. Its position (*mahall*) may be accusative as an exception (*istithna'*), or genitive as an apposition (*badal*), or nominative on the basis that the exception is disjunctive (*munqati'*), meaning: "But rather, those with whom you made a covenant among them at al-Masjid al-Haram."

**So long as they remain upright toward you, remain upright toward them.** That is, wait and observe their affair; if they keep to the covenant, then you keep to its fulfilment. This is like His saying ﴿fulfil their covenant to their term﴾, except that the latter is unrestricted while this one is restricted. The word **مَا** (*ma*) may carry the conditional sense or the verbal-infinitival (*masdariyyah*) sense.

**Indeed Allah loves the God-fearing.** Its explanation has already preceded.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 8:

﴿How﴾ is repeated to express astonishment at their steadfastness in the covenant, or at the continuation of its ruling, together with an alert to the cause. The verb is omitted because it is known, as in his saying:

Poetry:
"You two informed me that death is in the villages... so how (can it be), and here are this hill and this well?"

That is, "so how did he die?" ﴿And if they gain the upper hand over you﴾ meaning: and their state is that if they prevail over you. ﴿They do not observe toward you﴾ meaning they do not respect toward you. ﴿any bond of kinship (illan)﴾ — it is said to mean an alliance, and it is said to mean kinship. Hassan said:

Poetry:
"By your life, indeed your illan among Quraysh is like the illan of the young ostrich's foal among the ostriches."

It is also said to mean lordship (rububiyyah). Perhaps it was derived for the alliance from illan, which is the crying out, because when they made alliances they raised their voices with it and made it known. Then it was borrowed for kinship, because kinship binds between relatives what an alliance does not bind. Then it was extended to lordship and nurturing. It is also said that its derivation is from allal al-shay' (meaning he defined the thing), or from ala al-barq (meaning the lightning flashed). It is also said that it is Hebrew, meaning "God," because it was read as "Il," like "Jibra'il" and "Jibra'il." ﴿Nor any covenant (dhimmah)﴾ meaning a pact or a right, for whose neglect one is blamed. ﴿They please you with their mouths﴾ — this is a resumed sentence explaining their state, which is contrary to steadfastness in the covenants, and which leads to their not observing it when they prevail. It is not permissible to make it a circumstantial clause (hal) of the subject of "they do not observe," for after their dominance they do not please anyone; and because the intent is to affirm their pleasing the believers with the promise of faith, obedience, and fulfilling the covenant in the present, while concealing disbelief and hostility such that, if they prevail, they will spare no one; the circumstantial sense contradicts this, and their hearts refuse what their mouths utter. ﴿And most of them are defiant transgressors﴾ — rebellious, having neither a creed that restrains them nor a sense of honor that deters them. The specification of "most" is because some of the disbelievers avoid treachery and abstain from what leads to a reputation for evil. (p-73)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 9–10:

﴿They have exchanged the signs of Allah﴾ — they substituted the Qur'an (for something else). ﴿for a small price﴾ — a trifling worldly gain, which is following desires and appetites. ﴿So they have averted (others) from His way﴾ — His religion, which leads to Him; or the way to His House, by preventing the pilgrims and those who visit for ʿumra (ʿUmrah). The fa' (فاء, fa', the particle of consequence) indicates that their purchasing led them to obstruction. ﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ — their deed, this one, or what is indicated by His saying: ﴿They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship or covenant﴾. So the latter is an explanation, not a repetition. It has been said that the first (statement) is general regarding those who violate (their covenants), while this one is specific to those who made the exchange, who are the Jews, or the Bedouin Arabs whom Abu Sufyan gathered and fed. ﴿And it is those who are the transgressors﴾ — in wickedness.

﴿They have exchanged the signs of Allah﴾ — they substituted the Qur'an (for something else). ﴿for a small price﴾ — a trifling worldly gain, which is following desires and appetites. ﴿So they have averted (others) from His way﴾ — His religion, which leads to Him; or the way to His House, by preventing the pilgrims and those who visit for ʿumra (ʿUmrah). Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 11–12:

﴿Then if they repent﴾ from disbelief. ﴿and establish the prayer and give the zakat, then they are your brothers in religion﴾. They are your brothers in religion, having what you have and bearing what you bear. ﴿And We detail the signs for a people who know﴾ is an interjection urging reflection upon what has been detailed of the rulings concerning the covenanted (mu'ahidun) or the characteristics of those who repent.

﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant﴾ and if they break what they pledged to, namely faith (iman) or the fulfilment of covenants. ﴿And they revile your religion﴾ by plain denial and disparagement of its rulings. ﴿Then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, that is, fight them. The placing of "leaders of disbelief" in the position of a pronoun indicates that by this conduct they have become those with leadership and precedence in disbelief, deserving of being killed. It is said that the intended meaning of "leaders" is the chiefs of the polytheists, and the specification is either because killing them is more important and they are more deserving of it, or to prevent showing them leniency. ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Rawḥ on the authority of Yaʿqūb read ﴿a'immata﴾ with both hamzahs made clear, according to the original form; and making the yā' explicit is a grammatical error (laḥn). ﴿Indeed, they have no oaths﴾, that is, they have no oaths in reality, for otherwise they would not have reviled and would not have broken them. In this there is evidence that a dhimmi who reviles Islam has broken his covenant. The Ḥanafiyyah cited it to show that the oath of a disbeliever is not an oath, but this is weak, because the intended meaning is the negation of trust in them, not that they are not oaths, given His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And if they break their oaths﴾. Ibn ʿĀmir read ﴿lā aymāna lahum﴾ with the meaning "no security" (lā amān) or "no Islam" (lā islām), and whoever refuses to accept the repentance of an apostate has clung to it; but this is weak, because it may mean "they do not grant security" as information about specific people, or "they have no faith, so that they would be restrained on its account." ﴿So that perhaps they will desist﴾ is connected to "fight", that is, let your aim in fighting be that they desist from what they are upon, not the infliction of harm upon them as is the way of those who harm.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 13:

﴿Will you not fight a people﴾ is an exhortation to fighting, because the interrogative hamza (alif of inquiry) has entered upon the negation for the sake of reproach, and so it conveys emphasis in the action.

﴿who broke their oaths﴾ which they had sworn with the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the believers, that they would not support anyone against them; but they supported Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah.

﴿And they resolved to expel the Messenger﴾ when they consulted together about his affair in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of Quraysh), as has been mentioned in His saying: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾. It is also said that they were the Jews, who broke the covenant of the Messenger and resolved to expel him from Medina.

﴿And they began against you the first time﴾ with hostility and fighting, because he, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, began with them by calling them (to faith) and establishing the proof against them through the Book and the challenge (p-74) it presented; so they turned away from opposing him to hostility and fighting. Then what prevents you from opposing them and confronting them?

﴿Do you fear them?﴾ Do you abandon fighting them out of fear that some harm from them will befall you?

﴿Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ So fight His enemies and do not abandon His command.

﴿if you are believers﴾ For the requirement of faith is that none be feared except Him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 14–15:

﴿Fight them.﴾ This is a command to fighting, after the explanation of what makes it obligatory, and a rebuke for abandoning it, and a threat concerning it. ﴿Allah will punish them at your hands, and will disgrace them, and will help you against them.﴾ This is a promise to them that if they fight them, they will be victorious over them and will be empowered to kill them and humiliate them. ﴿And will heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, meaning the Banu Khuza'ah.

It is said: they were tribes from Yemen and Saba' who came to Makkah and embraced Islam, then they suffered severe harm from its people, so they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Be glad tidings, for relief is near."

﴿And remove the rage of their hearts﴾, on account of what they had suffered from them. Allah has fulfilled what He promised them, and the verse is among the miracles. ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾: this is a fresh statement that some of them will repent of their disbelief, and that indeed happened. It is also read as "wa-yatuba" in the accusative, with the particle "an" implied, so that it is among the things answered by the command, since fighting causes the punishment of one people just as it causes the repentance of other people.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of what has been and what will be. ﴿All-Wise﴾, who does not act or judge except in accordance with wisdom.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 16:

﴿Or did you suppose﴾ is an address to the believers when some of them disliked fighting. It was also said that it is addressed to the hypocrites. The particle "am" (or) is here disjunctive (munqati'ah), and the meaning of the interrogative hamzah in it is reproach for supposing. ﴿That you would be left alone while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove (jahadu) and did not take﴾ meaning: He has not yet distinguished the sincere (al-khulassa) among you, and they are those who strove, distinguishing them from others. He negated the knowledge while intending the negation of the thing known, for emphasis, since the knowledge being connected to it entails its occurrence. ﴿And did not take﴾ is coordinated (ma'tuf) upon "jahadu" and falls within the relative clause (silah). ﴿Any intimate (waliyah) besides Allah, His Messenger, or the believers﴾ meaning: an inner circle (bitanah) whom they befriend and to whom they disclose their secrets. What is in "lamma" of the sense of expectation (tawaqqu') serves as a reminder that the distinguishing of this is expected. ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ meaning: He knows your purpose in it, and this is like a clarification (mazij) for what might be imagined from the apparent sense of His saying: ﴿And Allah has not yet known﴾.

﴿It is not for the polytheists﴾ it is not proper for them ﴿to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾ any of the mosques, let alone the Sacred Mosque. It is said that the Sacred Mosque is what is meant. The plural was used because it is the qiblah (direction of prayer) of the mosques and their leading centre, so its maintainer is treated like the maintainer of all of them. This is supported by the qira'ah (recitation) of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub, who read it in the singular (masjid Allah). ﴿bearing witness against themselves to disbelief﴾ by openly displaying polytheism and denying the Messenger. This phrase is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) relating to the wāw (the plural pronoun "they"). The meaning is: it is not right for them to combine two contradictory things, maintaining the House of Allah and worshipping other than Him.

It is narrated that when al-Abbas was taken captive, the Muslims reproached him for polytheism and for severing the ties of kinship. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, spoke harshly to him. He (al-Abbas) said: "What is the matter with you that you mention our bad deeds and conceal our good deeds? Indeed, we maintain the Sacred Mosque, we are the keepers of the Ka'bah, we give water to the pilgrims, and we ransom the captives." Then this was revealed: ﴿Those, their deeds have become worthless﴾, namely the deeds in which they take pride, because of the polytheism that accompanied them. ﴿And in the Fire they will abide eternally﴾ because of it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 18:

(p-75)﴿Only he who believes in Allah and the Last Day, establishes the prayer, gives the zakat, and fears none but Allah, shall maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾ That is: their upkeep is only proper for those who combine the perfections of knowledge and of action. And among its upkeep is adorning it with carpets, lighting it with lamps, perpetuating worship and remembrance (dhikr) and the teaching of knowledge (dars al-'ilm) within it, and guarding it from what it was not built for, such as worldly talk. And from the Prophet (ﷺ) [it is reported]: «Allah the Exalted said: Indeed, My houses on earth are the mosques, and indeed those who visit Me in them are their inhabitants. Blessed is the servant who purifies himself in his house and then visits Me in My house; it is a right upon the one visited to honour his visitor.»

And the reason He did not mention belief in the Messenger (ﷺ) is that it is known that belief in Allah is accompanied by it and completes it, and by the indication of His saying ﴿and establishes the prayer and gives the zakat﴾ upon it. ﴿And fears none but Allah﴾ — that is, in matters of religion. For fear of dangers is an innate disposition that a sensible person can hardly restrain himself from. ﴿So it is hoped that those will be among the guided﴾ — He expressed it in the form of expectation (tawaqquʿ) to cut off the hopes of the polytheists of being guided and benefiting by their deeds, and as a rebuke to them by asserting that they are guided. For if these people, with their perfection, have guidance that revolves between "it is hoped" (ʿasā) and "perhaps" (laʿalla), then what of their opposites? And as a prohibition to the believers from being deceived by their conditions and relying upon them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 19:

﴿Do you consider the giving of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah?﴾ Al-siqaya (the providing of water) and al-'imara (the maintenance/tending) are verbal nouns (masdar) of asqa and 'amara. They cannot be compared with physical entities (al-jutath, "bodies"), so an elision (idmar) is necessary, its estimated form being: "Do you consider the people of the providing of water to the pilgrims as equal to one who believes," or "Do you consider the providing of water to the pilgrims as equal to the faith of one who believes." The first is supported by the reading of one who recited "suqat al-hajj wa 'umrat al-masjid" (the providers of water for the pilgrims and the visitors of the mosque). The meaning is a denial that the polytheists and their deeds, which are nullified, should be compared with the believers and their deeds, which are established. He then affirmed this with His saying: ﴿They are not equal in the sight of Allah﴾, and clarified their non-equality with His saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., the disbelievers are wrongdoers through polytheism and enmity toward the Messenger, peace be upon him, immersed in misguidance; how then could they be equal to those whom Allah guided and granted success to the truth and the right? It has also been said that the intended meaning of "the wrongdoers" is those who equate themselves with the believers.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 20–22:

﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the way of God with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank ( darajah) with God﴾ higher in status and greater in honor than those in whom these qualities are not combined, or than the people of the watering of the pilgrims (al-siqayah) and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque (al-'imarah) in your estimation. ﴿And those are the triumphant﴾ with the reward and the attainment of the good (al-husna) with God, not you.

﴿Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him, and of approval, and of gardens for them, wherein is enduring bliss﴾ in the Gardens, ﴿lasting bliss﴾ that is everlasting. Hamzah recited ﴿yubashshiruhum﴾ with the lighter form (al-takhfif). The indefiniteness of that which is given as good tidings (al-mubashshar bihi) indicates that it lies beyond specification and definition.

﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ He emphasized eternity (al-khulud) by the addition of "forever" (abadan), because the word khulud may be used for a long stay. ﴿Indeed, with God is a great reward﴾ before which what they earned for its sake, or the bliss of this world, is considered insignificant.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 23:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾ It was revealed concerning the emigrants (muhajirun), for when they were commanded to emigrate (hijrah), they said: "If we emigrate, we will sever ties with our fathers, our sons, and our clans, our trade will be lost, and we will be left destitute." It was also said that it was revealed as a prohibition against taking as allies the nine who apostatized and joined Makkah. The meaning is: do not take them as allies who would prevent you from faith and turn you away from obedience, due to His saying: ﴿if they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, meaning if they choose it and are eager for it. ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then those are the wrongdoers﴾, by placing allegiance in other than its proper place.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 24:

﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kindred (ʿashīrah)...﴾ — "your kinsfolk" (aqribāʾukum) — is derived from al-ʿishrah (companionship, close association). It was also said that it is derived from al-ʿashara (the number ten), since the ʿashīrah is a group that returns to a bond like the bond of ten. Abu Bakr read "wa-ʿashīrātukum" (ʿashīrātukum, plural), and it was also read "wa-ʿashāʾirukum" (ʿashāʾirukum, plural of plural).

﴿And wealth that you have acquired (iqtaraftumūhā)﴾ — you have earned it. ﴿And commerce, the slackness of which you fear (kasādahā)﴾ — the passing of the time of its brisk trade. ﴿And dwellings with which you are pleased — more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause﴾ — this is love by choice, not natural love, for that does not fall under obligation, since one cannot guard against it. ﴿Then wait until Allah brings His command﴾ — this is a response and a threat; "the command" is an immediate or deferred punishment. It was also said it refers to the conquest of Makkah.

﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ — He does not guide them to rectitude. In the verse there is a great severity, and few escape from it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 25:

﴿Indeed, Allah has given you victory in many battlefields﴾, meaning the places of battle, which are its positions. ﴿And on the day of Hunayn﴾. The place of the day of Hunayn [is also a battlefield]. It is permissible that it be taken as [governed by] an elided word, "in the days of battlefields," or that the "mawtin" (place) be interpreted as a time, like the "maqtal al-Husayn" (the killing of al-Husayn). The substitution of His saying ﴿when your great number pleased you﴾ for it does not prevent that it be coordinated (ʿatf) with the position of "fi" in ﴿battlefields﴾, for this does not require that the two share in what the coordinated term is attached to, so as to require their great number and its pleasing them in the gathering of the battlefields.

And Hunayn is a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims fought, and they were twelve thousand: the ten thousand who attended the conquest of Makkah and two thousand who joined them from the Tulaqa' (those freed at the conquest). [They fought against] Hawazin and Thaqif, who were four thousand. When they met, the Prophet ﷺ, or Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), or another of the Muslims said: "We will not be defeated today for lack of numbers," out of pleasure at their great number. They fought a fierce battle, and the pleasure and reliance of the Muslims on their great number overtook them, so they fled until their band reached Makkah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in his position, with none with him except his uncle al-Abbas, holding his bridle, and his cousin Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith. Consider this a testimony to the extremity of his bravery. He said to al-Abbas, who had a loud voice: "Call out to the people." So he called: "O servants of Allah, O companions of the tree, O companions of Surat al-Baqarah!" They turned back as one body, saying, "Here we are, here we are!" The angels descended, and they met the polytheists. He ﷺ said: "Now the furnace has become hot." Then he took a handful of dust and threw it at them, then said: "Flee, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" and they fled.

﴿Then your great number did not avail you﴾, that is, the multitude. ﴿anything﴾ of availing, or regarding the enemy's affair. ﴿And the earth became constricted for you despite its vastness﴾, despite its breadth, that is, its spaciousness: you did not find therein a refuge in which your souls could be at rest because of the severity of terror, or you could not stand firm in it, like one whose place does not contain him. ﴿Then you turned back﴾ to the disbelievers, your backs. ﴿fleeing﴾, defeated. And "al-idbar" is going backward, the opposite of "al-iqbal" (advancing).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 26–27:

(p-77)﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility (sakinah)﴾, that is, His mercy, by which they found calm and security. ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾, those who had fled. The repetition of the preposition (al-jarr) is to draw attention to the difference between their two states. It has also been said that they are those who stood firm with the Messenger, peace be upon him, and did not flee.

﴿And He sent down armies you did not see﴾ with your eyes, namely the angels. They were five thousand, or eight thousand, or sixteen thousand, according to the differing reports. ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾ by killing, capture and taking of captives. ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾, meaning that what was done to them was the recompense for their disbelief in this world.

﴿Then Allah relents after that to whomever He wills﴾ among them, by guiding them to Islam. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, He overlooks their faults and bestows favour upon them.

It is narrated: "(That some people from among them came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and embraced Islam, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are the best of people and the most righteous, and our women and children have been taken captive, and our property has been seized. Six thousand souls were taken captive that day, and camels and sheep were seized in uncountable numbers.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Choose either your captives or your property.' They said: 'We do not value anything above our lineages.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: 'These people have come to you as Muslims, and we gave them the choice between their offspring and their property, and they did not value anything above their lineages. Whoever has captives in his possession and is willing to return them, let him do so; and whoever is not, let him give us [what he has] and it will be a loan owed by us until we acquire something and then give him its equivalent.' They said: 'We are content and submit.' He said: 'I do not know, perhaps among you there are those who are not content, so instruct your leaders (ʿurafa') to bring it to us.' So they reported to him that they were all content.)"

It is narrated: "(That some people from among them came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and embraced Islam, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are the best of people and the most righteous, and our women and children have been taken captive, and our property has been seized. Six thousand souls were taken captive that day, and camels and sheep were seized in uncountable numbers.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Choose either your captives or your property.' They said: 'We do not value anything above our lineages.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: 'These people have come to you as Muslims, and we gave them the choice between their offspring and their property, and they did not value anything above their lineages. Whoever has captives in his possession and is willing to return them, let him do so; and whoever is not, let him give us [what he has] and it will be a loan owed by us until we acquire something and then give him its equivalent.' They said: 'We are content and submit.' He said: 'I do not know, perhaps among you there are those who are not content, so instruct your leaders (ʿurafa') to bring it to us.' So they reported to him that they were all content.)"

O you who have believed, the polytheists are but impure (najas) because of the corruption of their inner selves, or because it is obligatory to avoid them just as impure things are avoided, or because they do not purify themselves nor keep away from impurities, so they are generally engaged with them. In this is evidence that whatever is generally impure is impure (najis). And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that their very bodies are impure, like dogs. It was also read as "nijs" with a sukun on the ja' and a kasra on the nun, and it is like kibd in kabid, and it mostly occurs as a follower of rijs.

﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾ because of their impurity. The prohibition of approaching was stated for emphasis, or to prevent them from entering the Haram. It was said that what is meant by it is the prohibition of Hajj and 'Umrah, not of entering in every case, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him. Malik analogized all other mosques to the Sacred Mosque in the prohibition. In this is evidence that the disbelievers are addressed concerning the furu' (the derivative rulings of the Shari'ah).

﴿After this year of theirs﴾ meaning the year of Bara'a (Immunity), which is the ninth year. It was also said it is the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage.

﴿And if you fear poverty (ʿaylah)﴾ meaning want, due to their being prevented from the Haram and the cutting off of the gains and benefits that came to you from their arrival. ﴿Then Allah will enrich you out of His bounty﴾ through His gift or His favor in another way. He fulfilled His promise by sending down rain upon them abundantly, and He guided the people of Tabalah and Jarash, who embraced Islam and brought them provisions. Then He opened the lands and the spoils to them, and people came to them from all corners of the earth. It was also read as "ʿaylatun," either as a verbal noun like al-ʿafiyah, or as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl).

﴿If He wills﴾: He qualified it with the will so that hopes would be directed to Allah the Exalted, and to alert that He, the Exalted, is bountiful in this, and that the promised wealth would be for some and not others, and in one year and not another. ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing﴾ of your circumstances. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He gives and withholds.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 29:

﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day﴾ That is, they do not believe in them in the manner that is required, as we explained at the beginning of al-Baqarah (the Cow), for their belief is no belief. ﴿Nor do they forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾ That is, what has been established as forbidden by the Book and the Sunnah. It was also said that "His Messenger" refers to the one whom they claim to follow. The meaning is that they oppose the original basis of their religion, which has been abrogated (mansukh), in belief and in practice. ﴿Nor do they follow the religion of truth﴾ the established religion, which abrogates (nasikh) all other religions and nullifies them. ﴿From among those who were given the Book﴾ is an explanation of those who do not believe. ﴿Until they give the jizyah (poll tax)﴾ that which is imposed upon them to give; it is derived from "jazaa dinahu," meaning he repaid his debt, when he settled it. ﴿With willing submission (ʿan yadin)﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the pronoun, meaning: with a cooperative hand, in the sense of submitting; or "ʿan yadihim," in the sense of being Muslims who hand it over with their own hands, not sending it through the hands of others, and for this reason it was forbidden to appoint an agent for it. Or it means "from wealth," and for this reason it was said: it is not taken from the poor. Or it means "under a hand that dominates them," in the sense of being powerless and humiliated. Or it means "from the jizyah," in the sense of money handed over directly from hand to hand. Or it means "as a favour upon them," for allowing them to remain by means of the jizyah is a great blessing. ﴿And they are humbled (sagharun)﴾ meaning abased. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: the jizyah is taken from the dhimmi, and his neck is pressed (tuwjaʾu ʿunuquhu). The implication of the verse requires that the jizyah be restricted to the People of the Book, and this is supported by the fact that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, did not take the jizyah from the Magians until ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, may Allah be pleased with him, testified before him that the Prophet (ﷺ) had taken it from the Magians of Hajar. And he (ﷺ) said: "Treat them in the manner of the People of the Book (sunnu bihim sunnata ahl al-kitab)." This is because they have a semblance of a Book, so they are joined to the People of the Book. As for the rest of the disbelievers, the jizyah is not taken from them according to us, but according to Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, it is taken from them except the polytheists of the Arabs, based on what al-Zuhri narrated, that the Prophet (ﷺ) made a treaty with the idol-worshippers except those who were from the Arabs. According to Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, it is taken from every disbeliever except the apostate, and its minimum is one dinar each year, equal for the rich and the poor. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the rich pay forty-eight dirhams, the middle-income pay half of that, and the poor who earns a living pays a quarter of it, and nothing is due from the poor who does not earn.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 9, verse 30:**

﴿And the Jews said, "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah."﴾ Only some of their earlier generations said this, or some of those who were in Medina. They said it because, after the event of Bukhtnasar (Nebuchadnezzar), no one among them remained who memorized the Torah. When Allah revived him after one hundred years, he dictated the Torah to them from memory, and they marvelled at this and said, "This is none other than the son of Allah." The evidence that this statement was made among them is that the verse was recited to them and they did not deny it, despite their eagerness to deny things.

ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī and Yaʿqūb read ﴿ʿUzayr﴾ with tanwin (nunation), on the basis that it is an Arabic word, the predicate of which is "ibn" (son), not described by it. In the other reading (qirāʾa), its omission is either because it is not declined (diptotic) due to foreignness and definiteness, or because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters, treating the nūn like the letters of softness (ḥurūf al-līn), or because "ibn" is a descriptive term and the predicate is omitted, as in "our worshipped one" or "our companion." The last is rejected, because it leads to affirming the lineage while denying the predicate that is assumed.

﴿And the Christians said, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾ This is also the statement of some of them. They said it out of a conviction that a child could exist without a father, or because of what he did, such as healing the blind and the leper and raising the dead, which, they reasoned, could only be done by one who is God.

﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ This is either an emphasis on the attribution of this statement to them and a negation of any figurative meaning of it, or an indication that it is a statement devoid of proof and verification, similar to a meaningless word that exists in mouths but whose meaning does not exist in reality.

﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before.﴾ That is, their saying resembles the saying of those who disbelieved, so the genitive noun (mudāf) was omitted and the noun in the genitive (mudāf ilayhi) was placed in its position.

﴿Before⁠﴾ means before them. What is intended is their forefathers, in the sense that disbelief is ancient among them. Or it means the polytheists who said the angels are the daughters of Allah. Or it means the Jews, with the pronoun referring to the Christians.

The word "muḍāhāh" means resemblance, and the hamza in it is a dialectal variant (lugha). ʿĀṣim recited it with hamza, and from this is the saying "imraʾa ḍahyāʾ" (a woman who is ḍahyāʾ), on the pattern faʿīl, for a woman who resembles men in that she does not menstruate. The Arabic word ḍahyāʾ here is kept as it is discussed.

﴿May Allah destroy them⁠﴾ is a supplication against them for annihilation, for whoever Allah destroys is ruined. Or it is an expression of wonder at the monstrousness of their saying.

﴿How are they deluded?⁠﴾ That is, how are they turned away from the truth to falsehood?

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 31–32:

﴿They took their scholars and their monks as lords besides God﴾, by obeying them in declaring unlawful what God had made lawful and declaring lawful what God had made unlawful, or by prostrating to them. ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary﴾, by making him a son of God. ﴿Yet they were not commanded﴾, i.e., those who took lords, or those who were taken as lords, were not commanded, and this serves as evidence for the invalidity of such taking. ﴿except to worship﴾, i.e., to obey. ﴿one God﴾, who is God Most High. As for obedience to the Messenger and to all whom God has commanded to be obeyed, it is in reality obedience to God. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ is a second attribute, or a resumptive clause (isti'naf) affirming tawhid (the oneness of God). ﴿Glory be to Him above what they associate﴾, a declaration that He is far exalted above having any partner.

﴿They want to extinguish﴾, i.e., to put out. ﴿the light of God﴾, His proof indicating His oneness and His exaltation above having offspring, or the Qur'an, or the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿with their mouths﴾, i.e., with their polytheism or with their denial. ﴿But God refuses﴾, i.e., He does not approve. ﴿except to perfect His light﴾, by raising up tawhid and strengthening Islam. It has been said that this is an analogy for their state: in seeking to nullify the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) by denying it, they are like one who seeks to extinguish a great light spread across the horizons, which God wills to increase by His breath. The exception here is an incomplete exception (istithna' mufarragh), and it is valid with an affirmative verb because it carries the sense of negation. ﴿Even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾, its answer is omitted, because what precedes it indicates the answer.

﴿They took their scholars and their monks as lords besides God﴾, by obeying them in declaring unlawful what God had made lawful and declaring lawful what God had made unlawful, or by prostrating to them. ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary﴾, by making him a son of God. ﴿Yet they were not commanded﴾, i.e., those who took lords, or those who were taken as lords, were not commanded, and this serves as evidence for the invalidity of such taking. ﴿except to worship﴾, i.e., to obey. ﴿one God﴾, who is God Most High. He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion. This serves as an explanation of His saying: "And Allah refuses except that He perfect His light" [9:32]. For this reason He repeated "though the polytheists dislike it" [9:33 / 9:32]. However, "the polytheists" was put in place of "the disbelievers" to indicate that they combined disbelief in the Messenger with associating partners with Allah. The pronoun in "that He may make it prevail" refers to the religion of truth, or to the Messenger, peace be upon him. The definite article in "al-din" (the religion) is for the genus, meaning over all other religions, so that it abrogates them (fayansakhuha, i.e., naskh: abrogation, the supersession of one ruling or religion by another). Or it refers to their adherents, so that He humbles them (fayakhdhuluhum, i.e., abases them).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 34:

﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis (ahbar) and the monks (ruhban) consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾ they take it through bribery (rishwa) in rulings. The taking of wealth has been called "consuming" (akl) because it is its greatest purpose. ﴿And they avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾ His religion. ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah﴾ It is possible that by this is meant the many of the rabbis and monks, in which case it is hyperbole in describing them with greed for wealth and stinginess with it. And it is possible that what is meant is the Muslims who gather wealth and keep it and do not give its due right. Its being joined to those of the People of the Book who take bribes is for severe warning (li-l-taghlid). This is supported by the fact that when it was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, so ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Indeed Allah has not prescribed zakat except to purify with it what remains of your wealth." And his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever gives its zakat, it is not a hoard" (ma ud-diya zakatuhu fa-laysa bi-kanz), meaning, not a hoard for which a threat is made, for the threat concerning hoarding is coupled with not spending in what Allah commanded to be spent. As for his saying ﷺ: "Whoever leaves gold or silver [unpaid] will be branded with it" and similar, what is meant is the wealth whose right has not been paid, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, in what the two Shaykhs (al-Shaykhan) have related on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him: "There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its due right from it, except that on the Day of Resurrection plates of fire will be made for him, and he will be branded with them on his forehead, his side and his back." ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾ it is the branding with these.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 35:

﴿On the Day it will be heated in the fire of Hellfire﴾. That is, on the Day the fire will be kindled with intense heat upon them. Its original form is "it will be heated by the fire," but the heating (ihma') is attributed to the fire for emphasis; then the fire was deleted and the verb was attributed to the prepositional phrase (al-jarr wa'l-majrur, the prepositional phrase) to draw attention to the intended meaning. Thus the form shifted from the feminine (al-ta'nith) to the masculine (al-tadhkir). He said "upon them" (alayha) although the two things mentioned are (gold and silver), because what is meant by them is many dinars and dirhams, as 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Four thousand and what is below it is expenditure (nafaqa), and what is above it is a treasure (kanz)."

Likewise is His Exalted saying: ﴿and they do not spend them﴾. It has been said that the pronoun in both refers to the treasures or to the wealth, since the ruling is general, and their specification by mention is because they are the basis of acquiring wealth (qanun al-tamawwul). Or it refers to silver, and its specification is because of its proximity; the indication of its ruling is that gold is more deserving of this ruling. ﴿So their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with them﴾. Because their gathering and hoarding of it was in pursuit of prestige through wealth and enjoyment of delicious foods and splendid garments; or because they frowned at the beggar, turned away from him and presented their backs to him; or because these are the noblest of the outward limbs, for they contain the principal organs, which are the brain, the heart and the liver; or because they are the origins of the four directions, which are the fronts of the body, its rears, and its two sides. ﴿This is what you hoarded﴾, with the implied sense of "it will be said." ﴿For yourselves﴾, for their benefit, though it was the very cause of their harm and the reason for their punishment.

﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾. That is, the evil consequence of your hoarding, or what you were hoarding. It was also read as "taknuzun" with a damma on the nun.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 36:

﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾ means the total of their count. ﴿With Allah﴾ is the object governed by ʿiddah (the number), since it is a verbal noun. ﴿Twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾: in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), or in His decree. It is a qualifier of "twelve." His saying ﴿on the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾ is connected either to what is implied in it of the sense of establishment, or to "the Book" if the latter is taken as a verbal noun. The meaning is that this is a matter established in reality since the time Allah created the celestial bodies and the times. ﴿Of them, four are sacred﴾: one standing alone, which is Rajab, and three in succession, which are Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram. ﴿That is the upright religion﴾: that is, the prohibition of the four months is the straight religion, the religion of Ibrahim and Isma'il, upon them both be blessings and peace, which the Arabs inherited from them both. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ by violating their sanctity and committing their prohibited acts. The majority hold that the prohibition of fighting in them has been abrogated (mansukh, abrogated), and they interpreted the wrong as committing sins therein, for it is graver in burden, just as committing them in the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) and while in the state of ihram. It is narrated from ʿAta' that it is not lawful for people to make raids in the Sacred Precinct or in the sacred months except if they are attacked. The first view is supported by what is narrated: "that he, upon him be blessings and peace, besieged al-Ta'if and raided Hawazin at Hunayn in Shawwal and Dhu al-Qa'dah."

﴿And fight the polytheists all together, as they fight you all together﴾: all together. It is a verbal noun from "kaffa 'an al-shay'" (to restrain from something), since the whole is restrained from deficiency; it is placed in the position of a circumstantial accusative (hal). ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾: a glad tidings and a guarantee to them of victory because of their piety.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 37:

﴿Indeed, the postponing (al-nasi') is an increase in disbelief﴾. That is, the postponing of the sanctity of a month to another month. When a sacred month came while they were at war, they would make it lawful and make sacred another month in its place, until they abandoned the specific identity of the months and regarded only the number. It is also related from Nafi', through the transmission of Warsh, that he read (innama al-nasiyyu), by converting the hamzah into a yā' and assimilating the yā' into it. It was also read as "al-nasi" with its hamzah omitted, "al-nas'" and "al-nasa'," and all three are verbal nouns (masadir) of nasa'ahu, meaning he postponed it. ﴿An increase in disbelief﴾, because it is the making unlawful of what Allah has made lawful and the making lawful of what Allah has made unlawful, so it is another kind of disbelief which they added to their disbelief. ﴿By which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾, with an additional misguidance. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ﴿yuḍall﴾ in the passive form, and it is related from Ya'qub (yuḍill), with the verb attributed to Allah the Exalted. ﴿They make it lawful one year﴾: they make lawful the postponed one of the sacred months for a year and make another month sacred in its place. ﴿And they make it sacred another year﴾: so they leave it in its sanctity. It was said: the first to introduce this was Junadah ibn 'Awf al-Kinani, who would stand on a camel during the pilgrimage season and proclaim: "Indeed your gods have made the sacred month lawful for you, so make it lawful." Then he would proclaim among the tribes: "Indeed your gods have made the sacred month unlawful for you, so make it unlawful."

The two clauses are an explanation of the misguidance, or a circumstantial clause. ﴿That they may match the number of what Allah has made sacred﴾: that is, that they may conform to the number of the four sacred months, and the lam is connected to ﴿they make it sacred﴾, or to what is indicated by the whole of the two verbs. ﴿So that they make lawful what Allah has made sacred﴾, by matching the number alone without regard to the time.

﴿The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them﴾. It was also read in the active form, with Allah the Exalted as the agent, and the meaning is that He forsook them and misguided them, until they regarded the ugliness of their deeds as good. ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, with a guidance that leads to attaining right guidance.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 38–39:

﴿O you who believe, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the way of Allah," you grow heavy towards the earth?﴾ That is, you were slow. It is also read "tathaqqaltum" (you grew heavy), which is the original form, and "ithaqqaltum" is read as an interrogative for reproach. ﴿Towards the earth﴾ is connected to it, as if it were made to imply inclining and leaning, so it takes "ila" (towards). This was at the Battle of Tabuk, to which they were commanded after their return from al-Ta'if, in a time of hardship and summer heat, with the distance being great and the enemy numerous, so it was difficult for them. ﴿Are you content with the life of this world﴾ and its delusions, ﴿instead of the Hereafter﴾, that is, in place of the Hereafter and its bliss? ﴿Then the enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared with the Hereafter﴾, that is, how little is the enjoyment of it in comparison with the Hereafter? ﴿Except a little﴾, which is despicable.

﴿If you do not go forth﴾, that is, if you do not go forth to what you were called to, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ by destruction through a dreadful cause, such as famine and the appearance of an enemy, ﴿and will replace you with another people﴾, that is, He will substitute others in your place who are obedient, such as the people of Yemen and the sons of Persia. ﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾, since your reluctance does not diminish the support of His religion in any way, for He is free of need from everything and in every matter. It has also been said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger ﷺ, meaning, "And you will not harm him," for Allah, glorified and exalted, has promised him protection and victory, and His promise is true. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, so He is able to substitute and to change causes and to grant victory without aid, as He said:

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 40:

﴿If you do not help him, then Allah has already helped him﴾ meaning: if you do not help him, Allah will help him just as He helped him. ﴿When those who disbelieved drove him out, the second of two﴾ and there was with him only one man, so the response (jaza') is omitted and something that serves as evidence for it is put in its place. Or: if you do not help him, Allah has already made help for him obligatory, to the point that He helped him at such a time, so He will not forsake him at other times. The attribution of the expulsion to the disbelievers is because their intent to expel him or kill him was the cause of Allah's permission to him to go forth. It was read as ﴿thāniya ithnayn﴾ with sukun, according to the dialect of those who treat the defective noun like the quantitative noun in inflection, and its accusative is as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl).

﴿When they were both in the cave﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿when he was driven out﴾, a substitution of part (badal al-ba'ḍ), since what is meant by it is an extended period of time. The cave (ghār) is a hollow at the top of Thawr, a mountain to the south of Makkah at a distance of one hour's journey, where they remained for three days. ﴿When he said﴾ is a second substitute or an adverbial clause (ẓarf) relating to "second of". ﴿To his companion﴾, who was Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ with protection and aid.

It is narrated: "The polytheists came up above the cave, and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, became anxious for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What is your opinion of two whose third is Allah?' So Allah blinded them to the cave, and they began to circle around it, but they did not see him."

It is also said that when they entered the cave, Allah sent two doves, which laid their eggs at its base, and the spider, which spun its web over it. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility﴾, His security by which hearts find rest. ﴿Upon him﴾, upon the Prophet ﷺ, or upon his companion, and this is the more apparent, because he was the one who was distressed. ﴿And supported him with hosts you did not see﴾, meaning the angels, whom He sent down to guard him in the cave, or to assist him against the enemy on the Day of Badr, the Confederates, and Hunayn. Thus the clause is coordinated with His saying ﴿Allah has helped him﴾. ﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest﴾, meaning shirk or the call to disbelief. ﴿And the word of Allah is the highest﴾, meaning monotheism or the call to Islam. The meaning is that He accomplished this by delivering the Messenger ﷺ from the hands of the disbelievers to Madinah, for that was the starting point of it, or by supporting him with angels in these occasions, or by protecting and aiding him wherever he was present. Ya'qub read ﴿wa kalimatu Allah﴾ in the accusative, coordinated with "the word of those who disbelieved". The nominative is more eloquent, because it indicates that the word of Allah is high in itself, even if others surpass it; its superiority does not remain and is not regarded. For this reason he placed the separating pronoun in the middle. ﴿And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise﴾ in His command and His management.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 41:

﴿Go forth, light or heavy﴾ — lightly, in eagerness for it (linashatikum lahu), ﴿or heavy﴾ — reluctantly, on account of its hardship for you, or because your dependents are few or many; or mounted and on foot; or light and heavy in terms of weaponry; or healthy and sick. Accordingly, when Ibn Umm Maktum said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "Is it incumbent upon me to go forth?" he said, "Yes," until there was revealed ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾.

﴿And strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah﴾ — with whatever of these two you are able to, both of them or one of them. ﴿That is better for you﴾ than abandoning it. ﴿If you only knew﴾ — if you knew the good, you would know that it is good; or, if you knew that it is good, since Allah's report about it is true, then hasten to it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 42–43:

﴿Had it been a gain near at hand﴾, i.e., had what they were called to been a worldly benefit, ﴿and a journey of moderate length﴾ (qasidan), i.e., of middle distance, ﴿they would have followed you﴾, i.e., would have agreed with you. ﴿But the distance seemed long to them﴾, i.e., the journey that is covered with hardship. It is also read with a kasra on the ʿayn and the shīn (bi-kasr al-ʿayn wa'l-shīn). ﴿And they will swear by Allah﴾, i.e., those who stayed behind, when you return from Tabuk, offering excuses: ﴿"Had we been able, we would have gone out with you."﴾ They say: had we had the capacity, in terms of equipment or bodily strength. It is also read "lawu istaṭaʿnā" with a damma on the waw (bi-ḍamm al-wāw), likening it to the waw of the plural pronoun in His saying: ﴿they have bought error﴾ (ishtarawu al-ḍalāla). ﴿"We would have gone out with you"﴾: this stands in place of the answers to both the oath and the condition, and this is among the miracles, because it is a report of what occurred before it occurred. ﴿They destroy themselves﴾, by casting themselves into punishment. It is a substitute (badal) for "they will swear," because a false oath is casting oneself into destruction; or it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from its subject. ﴿And Allah knows that they are indeed liars﴾ in that, because they were able to go out.

﴿Allah has pardoned you﴾: an allusion (kināya) not to his error in granting permission, for pardon is among its implications. ﴿Why did you give them permission?﴾: an explanation of what was alluded to by the pardon, and a rebuke for it; the meaning is: for what reason did you grant them permission to remain behind when they asked you and made excuses with lies? Why did you not hold back?

﴿Until it becomes clear to you who are truthful﴾ in their excuse, ﴿and you know the liars﴾ in it. It is said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did two things for which he had not been commanded: his taking ransom (fida') and his granting permission to the hypocrites, so Allah rebuked him for both of them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 9, verses 44–45:

﴿Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your leave to strive with their wealth and their selves.﴾ That is, it is not the habit of the believers to ask you permission to strive, for the sincere (*al-khullas*) among them hasten to it and do not wait for permission to do it, let alone ask you permission to stay behind from it, or ask you permission to stay behind out of dislike of striving. ﴿And God is Knowing of the God-fearing﴾: a testimony to them of their piety, and His promise to them of His reward.

﴿It is only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day who ask your leave﴾ to stay behind. The specification of belief in God, Mighty and Majestic, and in the Last Day in both places (p-83) is to indicate that what impels one to jihad and restrains one from it is belief or non-belief in these two.

﴿Their hearts are in doubt, so in their doubt they waver﴾: they are bewildered.

﴿And had they intended to go out, they would have prepared for it﴾, that is, for the going out. ﴿equipment﴾ means readiness (uhbah). It is also read as ʿuddah(hu), with the ta' marbutah dropped when the word is in construct (idafah), as in the verse of the poet:

*Verily, the companions hastened the parting, so they departed,*
*And they broke faith with you in the matter they had promised.*

It is also read as ʿiddah(hu), with a kasra on the ʿayn when in construct, and as ʿiddatan without it.

﴿But God disliked their being roused to go out﴾. This is an istidrak (a corrective qualification of what is implied by the preceding statement). It is as if he said: they did not go out, but they were held back, because God disliked their inbiʿath, that is, their rising up to go out.

﴿So He held them back﴾, that is, He detained them with cowardice and laziness. ﴿And it was said: "Sit with those who sit."﴾ This may be a tamthil (a figurative depiction) of God casting the aversion to going out into their hearts; or the whispering of Satan commanding them to sit; or a report of some of them saying to others; or the permission of the Messenger, peace be upon him, for them. The word "those who sit" may include those with valid excuses and others. On both readings, the verse does not escape blame.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 47:

﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption﴾ by their going forth, not at all. ﴿Except corruption﴾, meaning mischief and evil. That does not entail that they have corruption such that, even if they had gone forth, they would have increased it, because the increase is considered in terms of the more general category from which the exception is made. Because of this assumption, the exception was taken as disjunctive (munqati'), but it is not so, because it is not an exception of the type called mufarragh (where the excepted item is left without an explicit general antecedent). ﴿And they would have hastened through the midst of you﴾, that is, they would have quickened their mounts among you with tale-bearing and sowing discord, or with defeatism and discouragement, from wada'a al-ba'iru wad'an, meaning the camel hastened its pace. ﴿Seeking to cause you turmoil﴾, meaning they would want to tempt you by bringing about disagreement among you or terror in your hearts, and the clause is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the pronoun in "awda'u" (they hastened). ﴿And among you are listeners for them﴾, meaning weak-minded people who hear their words and obey them, or tale-bearers who listen to your speech in order to convey it to them. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, so He knows their inner intentions and what proceeds from them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 48–49:

﴿Indeed, they had sought discord﴾ — meaning, the scattering of your affair and the dispersal of your companions. ﴿Before [this]﴾ — meaning on the day of Uhud, for Ibn Ubayy and his companions, just as they had held back from Tabuk after they had set out with the Messenger (ﷺ) as far as Dhu Jaddah, below the Thaniyyat al-Wada‘, they turned back on the day of Uhud. ﴿And they turned matters over for you﴾ — they devised for you schemes and stratagems, and they deliberated opinions aimed at nullifying your affair. ﴿Until the truth came﴾ — with victory and divine support. ﴿And the command of Allah prevailed﴾ — and His religion rose high. ﴿while they were averse﴾ — that is, despite their own displeasure. The two verses serve to console the Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers regarding their (the hypocrites') staying behind, and to explain what Allah restrained them for and disliked their setting out for, and to tear away their veils, uncover their secrets, and remove their excuses, as a remedy for what the Messenger (ﷺ) missed by hastening to grant them permission; for this reason he was rebuked over it. ﴿And among them is one who says: Grant me permission﴾ — to remain behind. ﴿And do not tempt me﴾ — do not cast me into temptation, that is, into disobedience and opposition, by not granting me permission. This implies that he will inevitably remain behind, whether he is given permission or not. Or [it means] into temptation through the loss of wealth and dependents, since there will be no one to provide for them after me. Or into temptation by the women of the Romans, according to what is narrated: that Jadd ibn Qays said, "The Ansar know that I am greatly fond of women, so do not tempt me with the daughters of the Yellow-skinned (p-84), but I will assist you with my wealth, so leave me [behind]."

﴿Surely, into temptation they have fallen﴾ — that is, the temptation into which they have fallen is this very thing: the temptation of staying behind, or the manifestation of hypocrisy, not that which they sought to guard against. ﴿And indeed Hell is encompassing the disbelievers﴾ — gathering them all on the Day of Resurrection; or [it means] now, because the encompassing of its causes around them is like its actual presence.

Al-Baydawi, *Anwar al-Tanzil*, commentary on Surah 9, verses 50–51:

﴿If good befalls you﴾ during some of your campaigns, ﴿a good thing﴾: victory and booty. ﴿It distresses them﴾ because of the excess of their envy. ﴿And if misfortune befalls you﴾ in some of them, ﴿a misfortune﴾: a breaking (of your strength) or hardship, as happened on the Day of Uhud (Uhud, the battle). ﴿They say, "We had already taken our precaution before"﴾: they boast of their withdrawal and seek praise for their opinion in staying behind. ﴿And they turn away﴾ from their gathering and speaking about this, or from the Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿While they are rejoicing﴾, delighted.

﴿Say: Nothing will befall us except what God has prescribed for us﴾, except what He has specially decreed and made obligatory for us of victory, or martyrdom, or what has been written for us in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz, the heavenly record), which does not change by your agreement or by your disagreement. It has been read as «هَلْ يُصِيبُنا» and «هَلْ يُصِيبُنا», and it is of the pattern فَيْعَلَ and not of فَعَلَ, because it is from the roots of the waw, as in their saying صابَ السَّهْمُ يَصُوبُ (the arrow hit its mark). Its derivation is from الصَّوابِ (rightness), because it is the occurrence of a thing in what was aimed at by it. It is said that it is from الصَّوْبِ (pouring down). ﴿He is our Protector﴾, our helper and the one who manages our affairs. ﴿And upon God let the believers rely﴾, because it is their duty not to rely upon anyone other than Him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 54–55:

﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger.﴾ That is: nothing prevented the acceptance of their contributions except their disbelief.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "an yuqbala" (that it be accepted) with the ya' (yuqbala), because the feminine marking of "al-nafaqat" (the contributions) is not real (haqiqi). It is also recited as "yuqabbala" (as the verb pertaining to Allah). ﴿And they do not come to the prayer except while they are lazy﴾ — mutathaqilin (sluggish, reluctant). ﴿And they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾ — because they do not hope for reward through either of them, nor do they fear punishment for abandoning them.

﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you﴾ — for that is a gradual lead-on (istidraj) and a ruin for them, as He said: ﴿Allah only intends to punish them through them in the life of this world﴾ — by reason of what they endure in gathering and guarding them of hardships, and what they see in them of distresses and calamities.

﴿And their souls depart while they are disbelievers﴾ — so they die as disbelievers, preoccupied with enjoyment, turned away from considering the outcome, and so that becomes a gradual lead-on for them. The root of zahuq (departure) is leaving with difficulty.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 56–57:

﴿They swear by Allah that they are indeed of you﴾ — that they are indeed among the body of the Muslims. ﴿But they are not of you﴾ — because of the disbelief of their hearts. ﴿But they are a people who are fearful﴾ — they fear that you will do to them what you do to the polytheists, so they display Islam out of taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation).

﴿Had they found a refuge﴾ — a fortress to which they could take refuge, ﴿or caves﴾ — hollows in the mountains, ﴿or a place to enter﴾ — a tunnel in which they could burrow and hide. It is a form of the verb (muftaʿal) from al-dukhul (entering), and Yaʿqub read ﴿mudkhalan﴾ from madkhal. It is also read "yajmazuna," and from it comes al-jamazah (a kind of swift running).

﴿And among them are those who find fault with you﴾ (yalmizuka), i.e., who criticize you, "concerning the charities" (al-sadaqat), i.e., concerning their distribution. ﴿If they are given from them, they are pleased; but if they are not given from them, behold, they are angered﴾. It is said that this was revealed concerning Abu al-Jawwas the hypocrite, who said: "Do you not see your companion? He distributes your charities among the shepherds of the sheep, and yet he claims that he is just."

It is also said concerning Ibn Dhi al-Khuwaysira, the head of the Kharijites: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was distributing the spoils of Hunayn, and he sought to win the hearts of the people of Makkah by lavishing the spoils upon them. He said: 'Be just, O Messenger of Allah!' He said: 'Woe to you! If I am not just, who will be just?'"

﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them﴾, i.e., what the Messenger gave them from the spoils or the charity. The mention of Allah here is for magnification and to draw attention to the fact that what the Messenger (peace be upon him) did was by His command. ﴿And said: "Allah is sufficient for us"﴾, i.e., His bounty is enough for us, ﴿"Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger"﴾, i.e., a charity or another spoil, ﴿"and His Messenger, [so He will give us more than He has given us]"﴾. ﴿"Indeed, we are turned toward Allah [in hope]"﴾, that He enrich us from His bounty. The whole verse is within the scope of a conditional, and its response is omitted, its estimated meaning being: "it would have been better for them." Then he explained the expenditure of the charities, as correction and affirmation of what the Messenger (ﷺ) had done, and said:
