Surah 9, verse 60 — Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil)

﴿Indeed, the alms (sadaqat) are only for the poor and the needy﴾ — i.e., the zakat is only for these enumerated categories, to the exclusion of others. This is evidence that the "criticism" (al-lamz) mentioned refers to their faulting the distribution of the zakat, not of the spoils of war (ghanaʼim). The faqir (poor person) is one who has no wealth and no earnings that meet his need, from al-faqar (the vertebra), as if his backbone had been struck. The miskin (needy person) is one who has wealth or earnings that do not suffice him, from al-sukun (stillness), as if incapacity had made him still. This is supported by (p-86) the words of Allah Most High: ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to needy people (masakin)﴾. It is also reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to ask for miskinah (neediness) and seek refuge from poverty (faqr). It has been said that the meanings are reversed, based on the words of Allah Most High: ﴿or a needy person in misery (matraba)﴾.

﴿And those employed to collect it﴾ — those who strive to gather and collect it.

﴿And those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾ — a people who have embraced Islam while their faith is still weak, so that their hearts may be won over; or nobles whose being given and being treated kindly may lead to the Islam of their peers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave for this purpose ʻUyaynah ibn Hisn, al-Aqraʻ ibn Habis, and al-ʻAbbas ibn Mirdas. It has also been said that they are nobles who are won over on condition that they embrace Islam, for he (ﷺ) used to give to them. The more correct view is that he used to give them from the one-fifth of the one-fifth (khums al-khums) which was his personal share. He counted among them those whose hearts are to be won over with some of it for fighting the disbelievers and those who withhold zakat. It has been said that the portion of the mu'allafah qulubuhum was for increasing the numbers of Islam; when Allah strengthened it and multiplied its adherents, that portion lapsed.

﴿And for freeing slaves (fi al-riqab)﴾ — and for spending in freeing necks, by assisting a mukatab (slave contracted to buy his freedom) with some of it to pay his installments. It has been said that it is by purchasing slaves and freeing them, and Malik and Ahmad held this view; or by ransoming captives. The shift from the preposition al-lam (li) to fi (in) indicates that entitlement belongs to the category, not to the individual slaves. It has also been said that it is to indicate that they have the greater right to it.

﴿And those in debt (al-gharimin)﴾ — those who are in debt for themselves, in what is not sinful and without extravagance, when they have no means of repayment; or for reconciling between people, even if they are wealthy, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Charity is not lawful for a rich person except for five: one who fights in the way of Allah, or one who is in debt, or a man who buys it with his own wealth, or a man who has a poor neighbour who gives charity to the poor man and the poor man gives a gift to the rich man, or an official who collects it."

﴿And in the way of Allah (fi sabil Allah)﴾ — and for spending in jihad by supporting volunteers and purchasing horses and weapons. It has also been said that it includes building bridges and public water reservoirs.

﴿And the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil)﴾ — the traveler who is cut off from his wealth.

﴿An obligation from Allah (fari'dah min Allah)﴾ — a verbal noun (masdar) for what the noble verse implies, i.e., Allah has enjoined the alms upon them as an obligation; or it is a circumstantial (hal) referring to the pronoun concealed in ﴿for the poor﴾. It is also read with the nominative, as "that is an obligation (fari'dah)".

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ — He places things in their proper places. The apparent meaning of the verse requires restricting the entitlement to zakat to the eight categories, and that it is obligatory to distribute to every category found among them, and observing equality among them is required by their being partners. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him. It was the view of ʻUmar, Hudhayfah, Ibn ʻAbbas, and others among the Companions and the Successors, may Allah be pleased with them all, that it is permissible to give it to a single category; this is the view of the three imams, and some of our companions chose it, and my teacher and my father, may Allah have mercy on them both, used to issue fatwas accordingly, on the basis that the verse explains that alms do not leave them, not that their division among them is obligatory.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 9, verse 61:

﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear."﴾ He hears everything that is said to him and believes it. He is called "an ear," a body part, for emphasis (*mubalaghah*, intensification), as if, from the excess of his listening, his whole being had become an instrument of hearing, just as the spy (*jasus*) is called "an eye" for the same reason. Alternatively, a verb is derived from it, *adhina udhunan* (he listened), as in *ani'a* and *shalila*. It is narrated that they said, "Muhammad is a listening ear. We say whatever we wish, then we come to him and he believes what we say."

﴿Say: "An ear of good for you."﴾ This is an affirmation to them that he is an ear, but not in the manner for which they blamed him. Rather, it is in that he hears what is good and accepts it. Then he explained this with His words:

﴿He believes in Allah﴾: he affirms Him, because of the proofs that have been established before him.

﴿And believes the believers﴾: he trusts them, because he knows their sincerity. The *lam* (in *lil-mu'minin*) is extra, to distinguish between *iman al-tasdiq* (belief as assent), which means acceptance and submission, and *iman al-aman* (belief as trust, granting safety). 

﴿And a mercy﴾: that is, he is a mercy.

﴿for those of you who believe﴾: for whoever shows faith, since he accepts it and does not expose his secret. In this there is an indication that he does not accept your words out of ignorance of your condition, but out of kindness toward you and compassion for you.

Hamzah read *wa-rahmatin* (with a *kasrah*) in the genitive, as a conjunction with *khayrin* (of good). It was also read in the accusative, as the cause of a verb implied by *udhunu khayrin*, meaning "he gives you permission out of mercy." Nafi' read *udhunun* with the lightened pronunciation in both places.

It was also read *udhunun khayrun*, with *khayrin* being an adjective of it, or a second predicate.

﴿And those who harm the Messenger of Allah, for them is a painful punishment﴾ for harming him.

(p-87) ﴿They swear to you by Allah﴾ in justification of their excuses regarding what they said or [for] staying behind. ﴿so that they may please you﴾, that you may be pleased with them; the address is to the believers. ﴿while Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾, that is, more deserving of being pleased [with] by obedience and conformity; the singular pronoun [in "pleased Him"] is either because the two pleasures are inseparable, or because the discussion concerns harming and pleasing the Messenger (ﷺ), or because the implied sense is "while Allah has more right that they should please Him, and so does the Messenger." ﴿if they are believers﴾, truly.

﴿Do they not know that﴾ that the matter [is such that] (anna al-sha'n, "that the matter is"); it is also read with the ta' (as a feminine verb form, "Do they not know that it..."). ﴿whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger﴾ acts in opposition (yushāqiq, a form of mufā'ala derived from ḥadd, "limit" or "boundary"). ﴿then for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein﴾: this is with the predicate omitted, meaning "then it is established that for him..." or with anna repeated for emphasis; it may also be coordinated with anna in "that he," with the answer (jawab) omitted, its estimated form being "whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger will perish." It is also read with the kasra, "fa-inna." ﴿That is the great disgrace﴾, meaning the everlasting destruction.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 64–65:

﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah will be sent down against them﴾ concerning the believers. ﴿Declaring to them what is in their hearts﴾ and exposing their concealed matters. It is also possible that the pronouns refer to the hypocrites, since the revelation concerning them is like the revelation sent down upon them, in that it is recited and used as proof against them. This indicates their wavering even in their disbelief, and that they were not firm in any matter concerning the Messenger ﷺ. It has also been said that it is a report in the sense of a command. It has been said that they used to say it among themselves in mockery, in reference to His saying: ﴿Say: "Mock, indeed Allah will bring out﴾ (i.e., reveal or disclose) ﴿what you fear."﴾ That is, what you fear of the revelation of a surah concerning you, or what you fear of its disclosing your faults.

﴿And if you ask them, they will surely say: "We were only conversing and playing."﴾ It is narrated: "A group of the hypocrites passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the expedition of Tabuk and said: 'Look at this man, he wants to conquer the palaces and fortresses of Syria. Far-fetched, far-fetched!' Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet of this, so he summoned them and said: 'You said such and such.' They said: 'No, by Allah, we were not engaged in any matter concerning you and your companions, but we were only engaged in what a riding party engages in, so that one of us might shorten the journey for another.'"

﴿Say: "Was it Allah, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?"﴾ This is a rebuke for their mockery of One at whom mockery is not valid, and a establishing of the proof against them. And do not heed their false excuse.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 66:

﴿Do not make excuses﴾: do not occupy yourselves with your excuses, for they are known to be false. ﴿You have disbelieved﴾: you have openly manifested disbelief by harming the Messenger (ﷺ) and attacking him. ﴿After your belief﴾: after your outward display of belief. ﴿If We pardon a group among you﴾: because of their repentance and sincerity, or because of their refraining from harm and mockery. (﴿We will punish a group, because they were criminals﴾): persisting in hypocrisy, or proceeding to harm and mockery. ʿĀṣim read both occurrences with the nūn (we). It was also read with the yā' and the active form with God as the agent in both, and ﴿If a group is pardoned﴾ with the tā' and the passive form, taking into account the meaning, as if he had said: "If a group is shown mercy."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 67–68:

﴿The hypocritical men and hypocritical women are of one another﴾ meaning: they are alike in hypocrisy and in being far from faith, like the parts of one thing (ka-abda' al-shay' al-wahid). It is said that it is a refutation of them in their oath by God, ﴿Indeed, they are of you﴾, and an affirmation of their saying ﴿and they are not of you﴾, and what follows it serves as evidence for it, for it indicates the opposition of their state to the state of the believers, which is His saying: ﴿They enjoin what is unacceptable﴾ (al-munkar), that is, disbelief and sins. ﴿And forbid what is acceptable﴾ (al-ma'ruf), that is, faith and obedience. ﴿And they withhold their hands﴾ from giving charity (al-mabarr), and the withholding of the hand is a metaphor for stinginess (al-shuhh).

﴿They forgot God﴾: they neglected the remembrance of God and abandoned His obedience. ﴿So He forgot them﴾: He abandoned them, withdrawing from them His kindness and bounty. ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾: the complete ones in rebellion and in transgression beyond the circle of goodness.

﴿God has promised the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein﴾, deeming the eternity (al-khulud). ﴿It is sufficient for them﴾ as punishment and recompense, and in this is evidence of the greatness of its torment. ﴿And God has cursed them﴾: He has removed them far from His mercy and humiliated them. ﴿And for them is a lasting torment﴾ that does not cease. What is meant by it is what they were promised, or what they suffer of the toil of hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 69:

﴿Like those before you﴾ meaning: you are like those who (came before you), or you have done the same as the deeds of those before you. ﴿Who were stronger than you in power, and greater in wealth and children﴾ is an explanation of their likeness to them and the portrayal of their state as the state of those others. ﴿So they enjoyed their share (khalaq) of worldly pleasures﴾ meaning their portion of the delights of this world. Its derivation is from khuluq (in the sense of measure, qadr), since it is what has been decreed (qudira) for its owner. ﴿So you have enjoyed your share, as those before you enjoyed their share﴾ is a censure of the earlier people for their enjoyment of their deficient portions of lusts, which are perishing, and their being diverted by them from considering the outcome and striving to attain the true delights, as a preface to censuring the addressees for resembling them and following their traces. ﴿And you plunged (khudtum)﴾ meaning you entered into falsehood. ﴿As those who plunged﴾ meaning as those (the people) who plunged, or as the company who plunged, or as the plunging that they plunged into.

﴿Those, their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾ they did not deserve any reward for them in either abode. ﴿And those, they are the losers﴾ who lost this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 70:

﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them: the people of Noah﴾ were drowned by the flood. ﴿And ʿĀd﴾ were destroyed by the wind. ﴿And Thamud﴾ were destroyed by the quake. ﴿And the people of Abraham﴾: Nimrod was destroyed by a gnat, and his companions were destroyed. ﴿And the companions of Madyan﴾, that is, the people of Madyan, who were the people of Shuʿayb, were destroyed by fire on the day of the shadow. ﴿And the overturned cities﴾ are the towns of the people of Lot, which were overturned with them, meaning they were turned upside down, so that their highest part became their lowest, and they were rained upon with stones of sijjil. It is also said that they are the towns of the deniers and the rebellious, and their being overturned means the reversal of their conditions from good to evil. ﴿Their messengers came to them﴾, meaning all of them. ﴿With clear proofs. And Allah was not one to wrong them﴾, that is, it was not part of His practice to do anything resembling human injustice, such as punishing without a crime. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾, in that they exposed themselves to punishment through disbelief and denial.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 71:

﴿And the believing men and the believing women are allies of one another﴾, in contrast to His saying ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another﴾. ﴿They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they establish the prayer and give the zakat, and they obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ in all matters.

﴿Those, Allah will surely have mercy upon them﴾ without doubt, for the sin (sa) is emphatic, confirming the occurrence. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾, dominant over everything, nothing can prevent Him from what He wills. ﴿Wise﴾, placing things in their proper places.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 72:

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and goodly dwellings in the Gardens of Eden﴾ [that the soul finds pleasant, or in which life is pleasant]. And in a hadith: they are palaces of pearl, emerald and red ruby.

﴿In the Gardens of Eden﴾: residence and eternal abiding.

And from him (ﷺ), upon him be prayers and peace: "Eden is the abode of Allah which no eye has seen and which has not occurred to the heart of any human. None dwells in it except three: the prophets, the truthful (al-siddiqun) and the martyrs (al-shuhada'). Allah the Exalted says: Blessed is whoever enters you."

As for the reference of the conjunction (al-'atf) in it, it may refer to the multiplicity of the promised [things], each one separately or all of them by way of distribution. Or it may refer to the difference in their description, as if He described it first as being of the kind of the most splendid places that they know, so that their natures incline towards it at the first moment it strikes their hearing. Then He described it as being enveloped in pleasant living, free from the impurities of turbidity, of which the places of this world are never free of some portion. And in it is what the souls desire and the eyes delight in. Then He described it as an abode of residence and stability, in the vicinity of ʿIlliyyin, where neither extinction nor change befalls them. Then He promised them what is greater than that, saying: ﴿And the good pleasure of Allah is greater﴾, because it is the origin of every happiness and honour, and the means to attaining arrival and winning the meeting. And from him (ﷺ): "Allah the Exalted says to the people of Paradise: Are you pleased? They say: And why would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have given no one else of Your creation? He says: I will give you something better than that. They say: And what is that? He says: I will let My good pleasure descend upon you, so I shall never be displeased with you ever."

﴿That﴾, i.e., the good pleasure, or all that has preceded. ﴿That is the great success﴾, in comparison with which the world and all that is in it are deemed insignificant.

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers ﴿by the sword﴾, and against the hypocrites ﴿by establishing the proof against them and enforcing the prescribed punishments﴾. ﴿And be harsh with them﴾ in that, and do not show them favour. ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾, their destination.

﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it]﴾. It is narrated that ﴿he (ﷺ)﴾ stayed for two months during the expedition of Tabuk, while the Qur'an was being revealed to him and he was censuring those who had stayed behind. Al-Jalas ibn Suwayd said: "If what Muhammad says about our brothers is true, then we are worse than donkeys." This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he summoned him, and he swore by Allah that he had not said it. Then this verse was revealed, and al-Jalas repented, and his repentance was good.

﴿They have indeed uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam﴾, and openly showed disbelief after openly showing Islam. ﴿And they resolved on what they could not attain﴾ of killing the Messenger (ﷺ). This was that fifteen of them agreed, upon his return from Tabuk, to push him off his mount into the valley when he ascended the ʿAqabah at night. But ʿAmmar ibn Yasir took hold of the halter of his mount, leading it, while Hudhayfah was behind it driving it. While they were in that state, Hudhayfah heard the clatter of camel hooves and the rattling of weapons, so he said: "Away with you, away with you, enemies of Allah!" and they fled. **Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on Surah 9, verses 75–76:**

﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and surely be among the righteous."﴾ It was revealed concerning Tha'labah ibn Hatib, who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Pray to Allah that He grant me wealth." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Tha'labah, a little that you can render thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." He returned to him and said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, if Allah grants me wealth, I will surely give to everyone who has a right his due." So he prayed for him, and he acquired sheep, which multiplied as worms multiply, until Medina could no longer contain them. He moved to a valley and cut himself off from the congregation and from the Friday prayer. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked about him, and it was said: "His wealth has increased so much that a valley can no longer hold it." He said: "Woe to Tha'labah!" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent two collectors (*musaddiqayn*) to take the charities (*sadaqat*). The people met them with their charities, and they passed by Tha'labah and asked him for the charity and recited to him the writing in which the obligations were set out. He said: "This is nothing but a poll tax (*jizyah*); this is nothing but a sister of the poll tax. Go back until I consider my opinion." Then the verse was revealed. Tha'labah came with the charity, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept it from you." So he began throwing dust on his head. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is your doing; I commanded you, but you did not obey me." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away. Tha'labah brought the charity to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), but he did not accept it. Then he came to 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) during his caliphate, but he did not accept it either. He died in the time of 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him).

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it﴾: they withheld the right of Allah from it. ﴿and they turned away﴾: from obedience to Allah. ﴿while they were refusing﴾: and they were a people whose habit was to turn away from it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 79:

﴿Those who slander﴾ is a predicate of blame (dhamm), either in the nominative (marfu', مَرْفُوعٌ) or the accusative (mansub, مَنصُوبٌ), or it is a substitute (badal, بَدَلٌ) for the pronoun in "their secret." It is also read as "yulmizuna" (يُلْمِزُونَ) with a *damma*.

﴿The volunteers﴾: those who volunteer (al-mutatawwi'in). ﴿from the believers in regard to charity﴾. It is narrated that: "The Prophet (ﷺ) urged people to give charity, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf came with four thousand dirhams and said, 'I had eight thousand. I lent four thousand to my Lord and kept four thousand for my dependants.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'May Allah bless you in what you gave and in what you kept.' So Allah blessed him, until one of his two wives agreed to take an eighth of the estate for eighty thousand dirhams. ʿAsim ibn ʿAdi gave a hundred wasq (وسق, a measure) of dates in charity. Abu ʿAqil al-Ansari came with a sa' (صاع, a measure) of dates and said, 'I spent my night drawing water with a rope for two sa's, so I left one sa' for my dependants and brought one sa'.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to scatter it over the charities. The hypocrites slandered them and said, 'ʿAbd al-Rahman and ʿAsim gave only for show, and Allah and His Messenger were certainly not in need of Abu ʿAqil's sa'. He only wanted to be mentioned, so that he might be given from the charities.'" Then it was revealed: ﴿and those who find nothing but their effort﴾, meaning except their capacity (taqah). It is also read with a *fatha* (بِالفَتْحِ), and it is the verbal noun of *jahada fi al-amr* (جَهَدَ في الأمْرِ), meaning he exerted himself in the matter.

﴿they mock them﴾: they ridicule them. ﴿Allah mocks them﴾: He repays them for their mockery, like His saying, ﴿Allah mocks them﴾ (Qur'an 2:15). ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ for their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 80:

﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾ He intends by this the equality of the two matters in not benefiting them, as he stated explicitly in his words: ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾.

It is narrated that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who was among the sincere believers, asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his father's illness to ask forgiveness for him, and he (peace and blessings be upon him) did so, and then the verse was revealed. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "I will surely increase beyond the seventy," and then the verse was revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will not forgive them﴾.

That is because he (peace and blessings be upon him) understood from "seventy" the specific number, since it is the basic one, so he allowed that this might be a limit beyond which the ruling would differ. So it was made clear to him that what is meant by it is multiplication, not limitation. The use of seven, seventy, and seven hundred and the like for multiplication has become widespread, because seven includes all the categories of number, so it is as if it were the whole number entire. ﴿That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾ indicates that despair of forgiveness and the non-acceptance of your asking forgiveness is not due to stinginess on our part nor to any deficiency in you, but rather to their lack of readiness, owing to the disbelief that turns them away from it. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, those who persist in their disbelief, and this is like the evidence for the preceding ruling, for the forgiveness of a disbeliever comes through giving up disbelief and being guided to the truth, whereas one who is immersed in his disbelief and sealed upon it does not desist nor become guided. It also draws attention to the excuse of the Messenger in asking forgiveness, namely that he did not despair of their faith as long as he did not know that they were sealed upon error. What is forbidden is asking forgiveness after knowledge, according to His exalted saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾.

﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their sitting [at home] contrary to the Messenger of God﴾ — "bi-maq'adihim" means by their remaining behind from the expedition, following him. It is said: "aqama khilafa al-hayy," meaning after them (i.e., after the tribe). It is also permissible that khilaf carries the sense of opposition (mukhalafah), in which case its accusative status is either as a reason (ʿillah) or as a circumstantial state (ḥal).

﴿And they disliked striving with their wealth and their lives in the way of God﴾ — preferring ease and comfort (al-da'ah wa al-khafḍ) over obedience to God. In this there is an implicit allusion (ta'ridh) to the believers who preferred, over these, obtaining His good pleasure by expending their wealth and their lives.

﴿And they said, "Do not go forth in the heat."﴾ — that is, some of them said to others, or they said it to the believers as a means of discouragement (tathbiṭan).

﴿Say, "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat,"﴾ — and you have chosen it through this opposition.

﴿if only they understood.﴾ — that their final return is to it; or that, whatever its nature is, they would not have chosen it by preferring ease over obedience.

﴿So let them laugh little and let them weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ — This is an announcement of what their condition will lead to in this world and the Hereafter. He expressed it in the form of a command to indicate that it is a decreed and binding necessity. It is also permissible that laughing and weeping are metaphors (kinayatan) for happiness and sorrow, and that by "little" is meant non-existence ('adam).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 83:

﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾ — that is, if He brings you back to al-Madinah, and in it there is a group of those who stayed behind, meaning their hypocrites — for not all of them were hypocrites — or those among them who remained. The ones who stayed behind were twelve men. ﴿Then they ask your permission to go forth﴾ — to another campaign after Tabuk — ﴿say: "You will never go forth with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me."﴾ This is a statement in the sense of a prohibition, for emphasis. ﴿Indeed, you were content with sitting behind the first time﴾ — this is a reason for it. Their removal from the register of the warriors was a punishment for them for their staying behind. ﴿The first time﴾ refers to the going forth to the campaign of Tabuk. ﴿So sit with those who remain behind﴾ — that is, with the ones who stayed behind, because of their unfitness for jihad, like the women and the children.

It was also read as "maʿa al-Khalifin" (with the Khalifin), with the alif shortened, i.e. "al-Khalifin" as "al-Khalifin" with qasr (shortened vowel) of al-Khalifin.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 84–85:

﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave.﴾ It is narrated: "(That ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy invited the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his illness. When he entered upon him, he asked him to seek forgiveness for him, and to shroud him in his garment that was next to his body, and to pray over him. When he died, he sent his shirt so that he could be shrouded in it, and went to pray over him, and then this verse was revealed.)" It is also said that he prayed over him and then the verse was revealed. The reason he did not forbid shrouding him in his shirt but forbade praying over him is that withholding the shirt would have been incompatible with generosity, and because it was a recompense for his having clothed al-ʿAbbas in his shirt when he was taken captive at Badr. What is meant by "prayer" (al-salat) here is supplication for the deceased and seeking forgiveness for him, which is forbidden with regard to an unbeliever. For this reason the prohibition is linked to the phrase ﴿ever﴾, meaning death in unbelief, for the bringing to life of an unbeliever is only for punishment, not for enjoyment, so it is as if he had not been brought to life. ﴿Nor stand at his grave﴾: do not stand at his grave for burial or for visitation. ﴿Indeed they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient﴾: this is a reason for the prohibition, or an explanation of the permanence of death.

﴿And do not let their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾: this is a repetition for emphasis, and the matter truly warrants it, for eyes are drawn longingly toward wealth and children, and souls are envious of them. It is also permissible that this be in a different context from the first.

It has been said that "the good things" refers to the houris, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿therein are good (khayrat), beautiful women.﴾ It is the plural of khayrah, a lightened form of khiyrah. ﴿And those—they are the successful (al-muflihun)﴾: those who attain their objectives.

﴿Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾ This explains what they have of the good things of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 90:

﴿And the excuse-makers among the Bedouins came, seeking permission to stay behind﴾. He means the tribes of Asad and Ghatafan, who asked permission to remain behind, offering as excuses hardship and the large number of their dependents. It is also said that they were the company of Amir ibn al-Tufayl, who said: "If we go out with you, Ta'y will raid our families and our livestock."

Al-Mu'adhdhirun (the excuse-makers) may derive either from ʿadhara (ʿudhr) in the matter, when one falls short in it while giving the impression that he has an excuse when he has none; or from i'tadhara (to offer an excuse), when one prepares the excuse, with the tā' assimilated into the dhāl and its vowel transferred to the ʿayn. The ʿayn may also be given a kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns, or a ḍamma for assimilation, but neither of these was read.

Yaʿqub read al-Mu'dhirun, from aʿdhara (to strive to produce an excuse). It was also read al-Mu'ʿadhdhirun with the ʿayn and dhāl both shaddated, taking it as from taʿadhdhara in the sense of i'tadhara; but this is a lahn (a grammatical error), since the tā' cannot be assimilated into the ʿayn. There is disagreement as to whether they offered excuses that were feigned or genuine. Then His saying ﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat back﴾ refers to others, namely the hypocrites of the Bedouins, who lied to Allah and His Messenger in claiming faith. And if they were the first group, then He called them liars by their offering of excuses.

﴿Those of them who disbelieved will be struck﴾ — from among the Bedouins or from among the excuse-makers, for among them are those who offered excuses due to their laziness, not their disbelief — ﴿with a painful punishment﴾, by killing and the Fire.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 91–92:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak or upon the sick﴾, such as the aged and the chronically ill. ﴿Nor upon those who find nothing to spend﴾ because of their poverty, such as Juhayna, Muzayna and the Banu Udhra. ﴿No blame (ḥaraj)﴾ means sin in lagging behind. ﴿When they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ through faith and obedience, in secret and in public, as a sincere supporter (al-muwali al-nasih) would act; or through whatever they are able to do, by deed or word, that returns to Islam and the Muslims with good. ﴿There is no way (sabil) against the good-doers﴾, meaning there is no blame upon them, nor is there any path to reproaching them. Rather, the phrase "the good-doers" was used in place of the pronoun to indicate that they are enrolled among the good-doers, not to be reproached for that. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ toward them, or toward the wrongdoer, so how much more toward the good-doer.

﴿Nor upon those who, when they came to you that you might mount them﴾. It is conjoined to "the weak" or to "the good-doers". They were the seven weepers from the Ansar: Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Sakhr ibn Khansa', Abdullah ibn Ka'b, Salim ibn Umayr, Tha'laba ibn Ghanama, Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, and Uluyya ibn Zayd. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have vowed to go out, so mount us on the patched shoes and the stitched sandals, that we may fight along with you." He (peace be upon him) said: "I do not find anything to mount you upon." So they turned away while weeping.

It is said they were the Banu Muqrin: Ma'qil, Suwayd and al-Nu'man. It is also said they were Abu Musa and his companions. ﴿You said, "I find nothing to mount you upon"﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the kaf in ﴿came to you﴾, with qad implied. ﴿They turned away﴾ is the response (jawab) of "when". ﴿And their eyes overflow﴾ means flow. ﴿With tears﴾, meaning tears; the min here is explanatory (li'l-bayan), and it together with its genitive is in the accusative position as a specification (tamyiz). This is more eloquent than "their eye overflows with tears", because it indicates that the eye has become a overflowing flood of tears. ﴿Grief (ḥazanan)﴾ is in the accusative as a reason (illa), or a circumstantial clause (hal), or an infinitive of a verb implied by what precedes it. ﴿That they do not find﴾: "lest they find" is connected to ﴿grief﴾ or to ﴿overflow﴾. ﴿What they might spend﴾ on their campaign.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 93–94:

﴿The way (of blame)﴾ is by reproach. ﴿is only against those who ask your permission while they are rich﴾, that is, possessing the means (of preparation). ﴿They are content to be with the women who stay behind﴾. This is a resumptive statement explaining what is the cause of their asking permission without an excuse, namely their contentment with baseness and their joining the company of those who stay behind, preferring ease. ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts﴾, to the point that they became heedless of the gravity of the consequence. ﴿So they do not know﴾ its outcome.

﴿They will make excuses to you﴾ for staying behind. ﴿When you return to them﴾ from this expedition. ﴿Say: Do not make excuses﴾ with false pretexts, ﴿for we will not believe you﴾, we will not accept you as truthful, ﴿since Allah has informed us of your news﴾, that is, He has made us aware through revelation to His Prophet of some of your news, namely the evil and corruption in your inner selves. ﴿And Allah will see your deed, and (so will) His Messenger﴾, whether you will repent of disbelief or persist in it; this is in effect a call to repentance and a grant of respite for repentance. ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, that is, to Him. The attribute is placed in the position of the pronoun to indicate that He is aware of their secret and their open conduct, and nothing of their inner thoughts and deeds escapes His knowledge. ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, by rebuke and punishment for it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 95–96:

﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may leave them alone.﴾ So do not rebuke them (...) ﴿So leave them alone.﴾ And do not reproach them.

﴿Indeed, they are filth.﴾ Reproach does not benefit them, for the purpose of reproach is purification by urging them toward repentance (inabah), but these are impure filth that does not accept purification. So this is the cause (ʿillah) for turning away and abandoning reproach. ﴿And their refuge is Hell.﴾ This completes the causal explanation, as if he said: they are filth from among the people of the Fire, for whom reproach in this world and the Hereafter is of no benefit. Or it is a second causal explanation, and the meaning is: the Fire is sufficient as a reproach for them, so do not burden yourselves with reproaching them.

﴿As a recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ It may be a verbal noun (masdar) or a cause (ʿillah).

﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them.﴾ By their oath, so that you continue toward them in what you were doing to them. ﴿But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiant people.﴾ That is, your being pleased with them does not entail the pleasure of Allah, and your pleasure alone does not benefit them if they are under the wrath of Allah and about to receive His punishment. Even if they are able to deceive you, they cannot deceive Allah, so He will not expose their concealment nor bring humiliation upon them. The purpose of the verse is the prohibition of being pleased with them and being deceived by their excuses, after the command to turn away and not to give them any attention.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 97–98:

(p-95) ﴿The Bedouins﴾ are the people of the desert (al-badw). ﴿Are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾ than the people of the settled towns, because of their wildness, their harshness, their not mixing with the people of knowledge, and their infrequent listening to the Book and the Sunnah. ﴿And more fitting that they not know﴾ means more deserving that they not know ﴿the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger﴾ of the laws, both their obligations and their recommended practices. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the state of every individual among the people of the tents (al-wabar) and the people of the towns (al-madar). ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He inflicts on their wrongdoers and their good-doers of punishment and reward.

﴿And among the Bedouins are those who take﴾ consider ﴿what they spend﴾ spend in the way of Allah and give in charity ﴿as a loss﴾ a penalty and a detriment, since they do not reckon it as a means of nearness to Allah, nor hope for reward for it, and they spend only out of showing off (riya') or out of dissimulation (taqiyya). ﴿And they wait for misfortunes to befall you﴾ the turns of time and its calamities, so that the matter turns against you and they are freed from spending. ﴿Upon them is the evil turn﴾ this is an interjected supplication against them with something like what they wait for, or an announcement of the occurrence of what they wait for upon them. The word "dā'ira" (turn) is originally a verbal noun or an active participle from "dāra yadūru," and it has been applied to the vicissitudes of time. "Al-sawi" with a fatha is a verbal noun, and it is made into an annexed construction for emphasis, as in your saying "rajul sidq" (a man of truth). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "al-sū'" here, and in the fath (the other reading) with a kasra... [the text reads: "وفي الفَتْحِ بِضَمِّ السِّينِ" — in the reading with fath, the sīn is with a ḍamma]. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of what they say when spending, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what they conceal.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 99:

﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day, and take what they spend as means of nearness (qurubat) to God﴾. The reason (sabab) for [the accusative of] ﴿qurubat﴾ is that it is the second object (maf'ul thani) of "yattakhidh" (takes). "Indeda of God" is either its attribute (sifah) or an adverbial complement (zarf) of "yattakhidh".

﴿And the prayers (salawat) of the Messenger﴾. The reason for his prayers is that he (ﷺ) used to supplicate for those who gave charity and ask forgiveness for them. Therefore it was prescribed that the one receiving charity should supplicate for the giver when taking his charity; but he is not to send blessings (yusalli) upon him, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O God, send blessings upon the family of Abi Awfa," because that is a rank (mansib) which belongs to him, so he may bestow it upon others as a favour.

﴿Indeed, it is a means of nearness for them﴾. It is a testimony from God to the soundness of their belief and a confirmation of their hope, given as a fresh statement (isti'naf) with the particle of alerting (harf al-tanbih, "ala") and "inna" which affirms the attribution, and the pronoun refers to their spending. Warsh recited ﴿qurbah﴾ with a damma on the ra'.

﴿God will admit them into His mercy﴾. It is a promise to them that mercy will encompass them, and the "sin" (the particle sa-) is for its certainty; and His saying ﴿Indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ is for its confirmation. It has been said that the first [group] refers to Asad, Ghatafan and Banu Tamim, and the second to 'Abd Allah dhu l-Bijadayn and his people.

﴿And the foremost, the first of the emigrants﴾ are those who prayed toward the two qiblahs (the two directions of prayer, first Jerusalem and then the Ka'bah), or those who were present at Badr, or those who embraced Islam before the Hijrah (the emigration from Makkah to Madinah). ﴿And the Helpers﴾ are the people of the First Pledge of al-'Aqabah, who were seven in number, and the people of the Second Pledge of al-'Aqabah, who were seventy, and those who believed when Abu Zurarah, Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, came to them. It was also read in the nominative (al-raf'), as a conjunction with ﴿the foremost﴾. ﴿And those who followed them in goodness﴾ are those who came after the foremost from both groups, or those who followed them in faith and obedience until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ by accepting their obedience and approving their deeds. ﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾ for what they obtained of His religious and worldly blessings. ﴿And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Ibn Kathir read it as ﻣِﻦ ﺗَﺤْﺘِﻬَﺎ ﺍﻷَﻧْﻬَﺎﺭُ ("min tahtiha al-anhar"), as he did in all other places. ﴿Abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

(p-96) ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾, that is, among those around your town, meaning Madinah. ﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾ — they are Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and Ghifar, who were settled around it. ﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾ is conjoined to (﴿among those around you﴾), or it is a predicate for an omitted subject whose description is: ﴿they have become obstinate in hypocrisy﴾. A parallel to omitting the described noun and placing the description in its stead is the statement of the poet:

"I am the son of Jala, and the one who ascends the heights..."

The description of the first (group) is for the hypocrites, and it is separated from it by what is conjoined to the predicate, or it is a new sentence explaining their persistence and proficiency in hypocrisy. ﴿You do not know them﴾: you do not recognize them by their persons. This is a confirmation of their skill in it and their refinement in avoiding the places of suspicion, to such a degree that their condition is hidden from you despite your complete discernment and true insight. ﴿We know them﴾, and We are acquainted with their secrets. If they are able to deceive you, they are not able to deceive Us. ﴿We will punish them twice﴾ with disgrace and killing, or with one of them and the punishment of the grave, or with the taking of zakat and the wearing down of their bodies. ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, that is, to the punishment of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 102:

﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾ and did not offer excuses for their staying behind with false excuses. They were a group of those who stayed behind who tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque when they learned of what had been revealed concerning those who stayed behind. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, entered the mosque as was his custom, prayed two rak'ahs, and saw them. He asked about them, and it was mentioned to him that they had sworn not to untie themselves until he untied them. He said: "And I swear that I will not untie them until I am commanded concerning them." Then the verse was revealed, and he released them.

﴿They mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾ They mixed the righteous deed, which is the showing of remorse and the acknowledgment of sin, with another evil deed, which is staying behind and agreeing with the people of hypocrisy. The waw (and) may be used with the meaning of the ba' (with), as in their saying: "I sold the sheep for a ewe and a dirham" (i.e., I sold the sheep in exchange for a ewe and a dirham). Or it indicates that each of the two is mixed with the other.

﴿It may be that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾ that He will accept their repentance, and this repentance is implied by His saying ﴿they acknowledged their sins﴾.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾ He overlooks the sins of the one who repents and bestows His favour upon him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 103–104:

﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾. It is narrated that when they were released, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth that kept us back, so give it in charity and purify us with it." He said: "I have not been commanded to take anything from your wealth," and then this was revealed. ﴿It purifies them﴾ from sins, or from love of wealth, which would lead them to its like. It is read as "tatahharahum" (from atharahu, which has the same meaning as tahharahu), and as "tuthahhirhum" in the jussive, as a response to the imperative. ﴿And it causes them to grow﴾, meaning it increases their good deeds and raises them to the stations of the sincere. ﴿And pray for them﴾, meaning show compassion to them by supplication and asking forgiveness for them.

﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾: their souls find rest in it and their hearts are reassured by it. It is put in the plural because the ones prayed for are many. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it in the singular. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their confession. ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their remorse.

﴿Do they not know﴾: the pronoun may refer to those who have been forgiven, and the intent is that it establish in their hearts the acceptance of their repentance and the reckoning of their charities; or it may refer to others, and the intent is to urge them to both. ﴿That Allah – it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ when it is sincere. It is construed with ﴿from﴾ because it includes the meaning of overlooking. ﴿And takes charities﴾: He accepts them in the manner of one who takes something in order to repay its equivalent. ﴿And that Allah – it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾: that it is part of His nature to accept the repentance of those who repent and to bestow favour upon them.

﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾. It is narrated that when they were released, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth that kept us back, so give it in charity and purify us with it." He said: "I have not been commanded to take anything from your wealth," and then this was revealed. ﴿It purifies them﴾ from sins, or from love of wealth, which would lead them to its like. It is read as "tatahharahum" (from atharahu, which has the same meaning as tahharahu), and as "tuthahhirhum" in the jussive, as a response to the imperative. ﴿And it causes them to grow﴾, meaning it increases their good deeds and raises them to the stations of the sincere. ﴿And pray for them﴾, meaning show compassion to them by supplication and asking forgiveness for them.

﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾: their souls find rest in it and their hearts are reassured by it. It is put in the plural because the ones prayed for are many. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it in the singular. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their confession. ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their remorse.

﴿Do they not know﴾: the pronoun may refer to those who have been forgiven, and the intent is that it establish in their hearts the acceptance of their repentance and the reckoning of their charities; or it may refer to others, and the intent is to urge them to both. ﴿That Allah – it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ when it is sincere. It is construed with ﴿from﴾ because it includes the meaning of overlooking. ﴿And takes charities﴾: He accepts them in the manner of one who takes something in order to repay its equivalent. ﴿And that Allah – it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾: that it is part of His nature to accept the repentance of those who repent and to bestow favour upon them.

(p-97) ﴿And say: "Work [as you will]"﴾, [meaning, whatever you wish]. ﴿Allah will see your work﴾, for nothing is hidden from Him, whether good or evil. ﴿and [so will] His Messenger and the believers﴾, for He, exalted is He, does not conceal from them [anything], as you have seen and it has become clear to you. ﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, by death. ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, by recompense for it.

﴿And [there are] others﴾ among those who stayed behind, ﴿deferred﴾, that is, delayed, meaning their matter is held in suspense, from arja'tahu, meaning "I delayed it" when you postpone it. Nafi', Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited ﴿murjawn﴾ with a waw, and both are dialectal variants. ﴿by Allah's command﴾ regarding their affair. ﴿Either He will punish them﴾ if they persist in hypocrisy. ﴿Or He will relent toward them﴾ if they repent. The alternation is with respect to the servants, and in it is evidence that both matters occur by the will of Allah, exalted is He.

﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of their states. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He does with them. It was also recited ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. The ones meant by these are Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya and Murara ibn al-Rabi'. The Messenger (ﷺ) commanded his companions not to greet them or speak to them. When they saw that, they sincerely purified their intentions and entrusted their affair to Allah, so Allah, exalted is He, had mercy on them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 107:

﴿And those who took a mosque⟩ is conjoined to ﴿and others held in suspense⟩ (al-Tawba 9:106), or it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted, meaning: "and among those we have described are those who took [a mosque]." Or it is in the accusative on the principle of specification (al-ikhtisas). Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿ḍirāran﴾ without the conjunction "wa" (i.e., ﴿ḍirāran﴾ rather than ﴿wa-ḍirāran﴾ ... as a separate item), [meaning] causing harm to the believers.

It is related: "When the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf built the Mosque of Quba', they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to come to them, so he came and prayed in it. Their brothers, the Banu Ghanm ibn 'Awf, envied them, so they built a mosque with the intention that Abu 'Amir the monk would lead them in it when he arrived from Syria. When they had completed it, they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'We have built a mosque for the one who has need, the sick, the night of rain and the cold. So pray in it, so that we may take it as a place of prayer.' He took his garment to stand with them, and [the verse] was revealed. He summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, Ma'n ibn 'Adi, 'Amir ibn al-Sakan and al-Wahshi, and said to them: 'Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it.' It was done, and in its place a rubbish dump was made."

﴿And disbelief﴾ and a strengthening of the disbelief they harbour. ﴿And division among the believers﴾ meaning, among those who used to gather for prayer at the Mosque of Quba'. ﴿And as an ambush﴾ i.e., a waiting in readiness. ﴿For him who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾ meaning Abu 'Amir the monk, for he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uhud: "I find no people fighting you except that I will fight you alongside them." He continued fighting him until the day of Hunayn, until he was defeated with Hawazin and fled to Syria to bring troops from Caesar with which to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He died alone at Qinnasrin. It is also said that he was gathering armies on the day of the Confederates, and when they were defeated he went out to Syria. ("And before") is related either to ﴿warred﴾ or to ﴿took﴾, i.e., they took a mosque before these people hypocritically stayed behind, for it is related that "it was built shortly before the Battle of Tabuk, and they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to come to it. He said: 'I am on the verge of a journey; when we return, if Allah wills, we will pray in it.' When he returned, they repeated the request to him, and [the verse] was revealed."

﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good"﴾: we intended by its construction nothing but the good quality, or the good intention, which is prayer, remembrance, and providing room for those who pray. ﴿And Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾ in their oath.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 108:

﴿Never stand in it﴾ for prayer. ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day﴾ means the Mosque of Qiba' (Quba), which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) founded and in which he prayed during the days of his stay at Qiba' from Monday to Friday, because it is more fitting to the narrative. Or it means the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), following the statement of Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him): "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and he said, 'It is your mosque, this mosque of Medina.'"

﴿From the first day﴾ means from the first of the days of its existence. And "from" (min) here covers both time and place, as in his saying:

*Whose are these abodes at the peak of al-Hajar?*
*Worn away by generations and by ages.*

﴿It is more worthy that you stand in it﴾ means it is more deserving that you pray in it. ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾ from sins and blameworthy traits, seeking the good pleasure of Allah, glorified and exalted be He. It was also said: from major impurity (janabah), so that they do not sleep in a state of it. ﴿And Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾: He is pleased with them and draws them near to His presence, as a lover draws near his beloved.

It was said: "When this was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, and the Muhajirun with him, until he stopped at the door of the Mosque of Qiba'. There he found the Ansar sitting, and he (peace be upon him) said, 'Are you believers?' They remained silent. He asked again, and 'Umar said, 'They are believers, and I am with them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Are you content with the decree?' They said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Are you patient in calamity?' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Are you thankful in ease?' They said, 'Yes.' Then he (ﷺ) said, 'You are believers, by the Lord of the Ka'bah.' He sat down and then said, 'O assembly of the Ansar, Allah, mighty and majestic, has praised you. What do you do when performing ablution and when relieving yourselves?' They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we follow excrement with three stones, then we follow the stones with water.' Then he recited: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves.﴾"

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 109:

﴿Is he, then, who founded his building﴾ — the building of his religion. ﴿upon piety from Allah and [seeking] His good pleasure, better﴾ — upon a firm foundation, which is piety from Allah and seeking His good pleasure through obedience. ﴿Or he who founded his building upon the brink of a crumbling precipice﴾ — upon a foundation that is the weakest and most fragile of foundations. ﴿so that it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾ — its weakness and his lack of firm support led him to fall into the Fire. He placed "the brink of a precipice," which is what a rushing torrent has eroded, opposite piety, as an illustration of what they built their religious affair upon: its falsehood and its swift effacement. Then he made the image more specific by [mentioning] its collapse with him into the Fire, and he placed it opposite "good pleasure," as a warning that founding that [building] upon something that protects him from the Fire and brings him to the good pleasure of Allah and its requirements, the least of which is Paradise. And founding this [building] upon what they are engaged in, [which places them] on the verge of falling into the Fire moment by moment, while their ultimate destination is the Fire without doubt.

Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read (usussa) (ُأسِّسَ) in the passive voice. It was also read as (asasa bunyanihi) and (asasa bunyanihi) with the genitive construction, and (assa) and (asa'a) with a fatha and a long vowel, and (issa) with a kasra; all three are plural forms of (ass), meaning foundation. (Taqwa) is read with tanwin, the alif being for lengthening (ilhaq) and not for feminine marking, as in (tatra). Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and Abu Bakr read (judurfin) (ﺟُﺮُفٍ) with lightening of the middle radical. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ — to that in which lies their welfare and salvation.

﴿Their building which they built will not cease﴾ — "bināʾuhum" (their building) which "banaw" (they built) is a *maṣdar* (verbal noun, used here to mean the object built), and it is not a plural. For this reason the feminine ta' (ة) may be attached to it, and it is described with a singular adjective and has a predicate given in the singular, ﴿a doubt in their hearts﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy. The meaning is that this building of theirs will not cease to be the cause of their doubt and the increase of their hypocrisy, for it was what led them to that. Then, when the Messenger (ﷺ) demolished it, that became firmly rooted in their hearts and increased, to the point that its mark does not leave their hearts. ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, into fragments such that they no longer have the capacity for perception or inner awareness. This is in the utmost degree of emphasis, and the exception (*istithnāʾ*) is from the most general of times. It was said that the meaning of "cutting" is what will happen through being killed, or in the grave, or in the Fire. It was also said that the "cutting" is through repentance, out of regret and sorrow.

Yaʿqūb read "ilā" with the particle of limit (*ḥarf al-intihāʾ*), and "taqaṭṭaʿa" with the meaning of "tataqaṭṭaʿa," and this is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and Ḥafs. It was also read as "yaqṭaʿu" with the *yāʾ*, and "tuqṭaʿa" with the lightened form, and "taqaṭṭaʿa qulūbuhum" addressed to the Messenger, or to every addressee; and "wa-law quṭṭiʿat" and "wa-law quṭṭiʿat" with the form for the active and passive voice (*al-binaʾ lil-fāʿil wal-maf‌ʿūl*).

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their intentions. ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He commanded regarding the demolition of their building.

(p-99) ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth, in return for which they shall have Paradise.﴾ This is an allegory for God's rewarding them with Paradise in exchange for their expending their lives and their wealth in His way. ﴿They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed.﴾ This is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) explaining the purpose for which the purchase was made. It has also been said that "yuqatiluna" (they fight) is in the sense of a command. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read the passive form (yuqtalun) with its verb placed first, i.e., "wa-yuqtalun fa-yaqtulun" [they are killed and they kill]. You already know that the conjunction "wa" (and) does not necessarily imply sequence, and that the action of some may be attributed to all. ﴿A promise binding upon Him, true﴾: this is an emphatic infinitive (masdar mu'akkid) for what the purchase implies, since it carries the meaning of a promise. ﴿In the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an﴾, being mentioned in both of them as it is affirmed in the Qur'an. ﴿And who is truer to his covenant than Allah?﴾ This is an intensification of His fulfilling it and an affirmation that it is true. ﴿So rejoice in the bargain you have made, which you have concluded with Him.﴾ Be overjoyed with it to the utmost degree, for it has made necessary for you great objectives, as He said: ﴿And that is the great triumph.﴾

**﴿The repenters﴾** is in the nominative for praise (al-madh, the laudatory construction), meaning: they are the repenters. What is meant by them is the believers already mentioned. It is also permissible for it to be a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is omitted, the estimate being: "the repenters are among the people of Paradise, even if they did not fight," because of His saying: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best reward﴾. Or its predicate is what follows it, meaning: those who truly repent of disbelief are the ones who combine these qualities.

It has been read with the ya' in the accusative (naṣb), as praise, or in the genitive (jarr) as an attributive adjective (ṣifah) of "the believers."

**﴿The worshippers﴾** are those who worship Allah, sincerely devoting the religion to Him.

**﴿The praisers﴾** are those who praise Him for His blessings, or for what befalls them of ease and hardship.

**﴿The wanderers﴾** are those who fast. This is based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The wandering of my community is fasting." It is so called because fasting restrains one from desires, or because it is a spiritual discipline (riyāḍah) through which one attains knowledge of the hidden realms of the dominion (al-mulk) and the unseen kingdom (al-malakūt). Alternatively, "the wanderers" means those who wander for jihad (struggle in the way of Allah) or for seeking knowledge.

**﴿Those who bow and prostrate﴾** refers to prayer.

**﴿Those who enjoin what is right﴾** means enjoining faith and obedience.

**﴿And those who forbid what is wrong﴾** means forbidding polytheism and sins. The conjunction (al-'āṭif) here is to indicate that what is joined to it is, in ruling, one single quality, as if He had said: "those who combine the two descriptions."

In His saying ﴿and those who guard the limits of Allah﴾, the meaning is: what lies between Him and His servants of the realities and the laws. This serves to alert that what precedes is the detailed enumeration of virtues, and this is their summary. It has been said that this is to announce that the enumeration is complete with the seventh, since seven is the complete number, and the eighth begins another enumeration joined to it; for this reason it is called the "waw of eight" (waw al-thamāniyah).

**﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾**: meaning those described with these virtues. The word "the believers" is placed in the position of their pronoun to alert that their faith called them to this, and that the complete believer is one who is like this. The object of the good tidings is omitted for magnification, as if it were said: "give them tidings of what is too great to be grasped by understanding or expressed by speech."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 113–114:

﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾ It is narrated: "When death approached Abu Talib, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: 'Say a word by which I may argue on your behalf before Allah.' But he refused. So the Prophet (ﷺ), upon him be prayer and peace, said: 'I will continue to ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from it.' Then this was revealed." It was also said that when he conquered Makkah, he went out to al-Abwa', visited the grave of his mother, then stood weeping and said: "I asked my Lord for permission to visit the grave of my mother, and He permitted me. I asked Him for permission to ask forgiveness for her, but He did not permit me, and He revealed to me these two verses."

﴿And even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ — that is, by their dying in disbelief. In this is evidence for the permissibility of asking forgiveness for them while they are alive, for it is a request for their guidance to faith. By this the objection is answered regarding Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) asking forgiveness for his disbelieving father, when he said: (p-100) ﴿And the request of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾. Ibrahim had promised his father with his words: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾, that is, I will surely seek your forgiveness by [seeking] your guidance to faith, for faith erases what came before it. This is supported by the reading of whoever read "abahu" (his father), or "wa'adaha Ibrahima abuhu" (his father promised it to Ibrahim), and it is the promise of faith. ﴿Then when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah﴾ — by his dying in disbelief, or it was revealed to him that he would never believe — ﴿he disassociated himself from him﴾, he ceased his asking forgiveness. ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was tender-hearted﴾, greatly sorrowful, and this is a metaphor for the extent of his compassion and the tenderness of his heart. ﴿Forbearing﴾, patient with harm. The clause explains what moved him to ask forgiveness for him despite his harshness toward him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 115–116:

﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray﴾ meaning: [He would not] call them misguided (ḍullāl) and hold them to account in the manner of such accountability after He had guided them to Islam. ﴿until He makes clear to them what they should beware of﴾ until He makes clear to them the prohibition of what must be avoided (ḥaẓr mā yajibu ittiqāʾuhu). This seems to be an explanation of the excuse of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his saying to his uncle, or to those who sought forgiveness for their polytheist forebears before the prohibition was issued. It has also been said that it concerns a people who persisted in the earlier ruling regarding the qibla, wine, and the like. In general, it is evidence that the heedless person is not held responsible. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾, so He knows their state in both circumstances.

﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have, besides Allah, no protector or helper.﴾ When He forbade them from seeking forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives, and this included the obligation of disassociating from them entirely, He made clear to them that Allah is the owner of every existing thing, the one who manages its affairs and is dominant over it, and that no guardianship or support can be obtained by them except from Him, so that they would turn wholeheartedly toward Him and disavow everything other than Him, until no aim remains for them in what they do or refrain from besides Him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 9, verse 117:

﴿Certainly Allah turned in mercy to the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾ concerning the permission the hypocrites had sought to stay behind, or He cleared them of the stain of sins, like His saying, ﴿that Allah may forgive you your past and future sins﴾. It was also said: it means He roused them to repentance (tawbah). The meaning is: there is no one who does not need to repent, even the Prophet (ﷺ), the Emigrants and the Helpers, because of His saying, ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you﴾. For there is no one who does not have a station beyond which he sees a deficiency in what he is in, and his ascent toward it is a repentance from that deficiency, and a manifestation of its excellence, since it is the station of the prophets and the righteous among His servants. ﴿Who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, at its time, which was their condition in the expedition of Tabuk. They were in a hardship of provisions: ten men would take turns on one camel, and the provisions were so scarce that it was said that two men would share a single date, and water, until they drank the *fazz* (a stomach-bag of water taken from a camel's stomach). ﴿After the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved﴾ from steadfastness in faith or from following the Messenger (peace be upon him). In ﴿kāda﴾ there is either the *ḍamīr al-sha'n* (the pronoun of the matter, "it") or the pronoun of the people, and what refers back to it is the pronoun in ﴿minhum﴾ (of them). Ḥamzah and Ḥafṣ read ﴿yazīgh﴾ with the *yā'* (the masculine form), because the feminine gender of "hearts" is not real (not grammatically true feminine). It was also read: "after the hearts of a group of them had swerved," meaning the ones who stayed behind. ﴿Then He turned to them in mercy﴾: a repetition for emphasis, and an alert that He turned to them because of what they endured of hardship; or it is meant that He turned to them because of their tender affection (*kaydūdah*). ﴿Indeed He is, toward them, Most Kind, Most Merciful﴾.

(p-101) ﴿And upon the three﴾ He also turned in mercy to the three: Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn al-Rabi'. ﴿Who were left behind﴾ They stayed behind from the expedition (ghazw), or their matter was deferred (khalafa amruhum); they are the Murji'un (those who defer judgment). ﴿Until, when the earth became straitened for them despite its vastness﴾ That is, despite its spaciousness (bi-rahabiha), because people had turned away from them entirely; this is a metaphor for extreme bewilderment. ﴿And their souls became straitened for them﴾ meaning their hearts, from the excess of loneliness and grief, such that neither companionship nor joy could contain them. ﴿And they perceived﴾ and knew. ﴿That there is no refuge from Allah﴾ from His wrath. ﴿Except in Him﴾ except in seeking His forgiveness. ﴿Then He turned to them in mercy﴾ by granting them success in repentance. ﴿That they might repent﴾ or He sent down the acceptance of their repentance so that they would be counted among those who repent; or He turned to them with acceptance and mercy again and again, so that they would remain steadfast in their repentance. ﴿Indeed Allah is the Accepter of repentance﴾ for whoever repents, even if he returns [to sin] a hundred times in a single day. ﴿The Merciful﴾ who bestows favors upon them with blessings.
