Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 120:

﴿It was not fitting for the people of Madinah and the Bedouins around them to stay behind from the Messenger of God﴾ This is a prohibition expressed in the form of a negation, for emphasis. ﴿Nor to prefer their own selves over his self﴾ i.e., nor to spare themselves from what he did not spare himself from, and to endure with him what he endures of hardships.

It is narrated: "Abu Khaythama reached his orchard, and he had a beautiful wife who had spread out for him in the shade, laid down the mat for him, and brought him dates and cold water. He looked and said: 'A shaded shade, ripe dates, cold water, and a beautiful woman, while the Messenger of God ﷺ is in the sun and the wind. This is not good.' He stood up, saddled his she-camel, took his sword and his spear, and went off like the wind. The Messenger of God ﷺ cast his gaze toward the road, and behold, a rider appeared to him through the mirage. He said: 'Be Abu Khaythama,' and it was indeed him. The Messenger of God ﷺ rejoiced at him and asked forgiveness for him."

In (لا يَرْغَبُوا) both the accusative (naṣb) and the jussive (jazm) are permissible. ﴿That﴾ refers to what is indicated by His saying "it was not fitting," namely the prohibition against staying behind or the obligation to accompany him. ﴿Because﴾ means "by reason that." ﴿Thirst will not afflict them﴾ i.e., any measure of thirst. ﴿Nor fatigue﴾ i.e., weariness. ﴿Nor hunger﴾ i.e., famine. ﴿In the way of God, nor do they tread﴾ i.e., nor do they step upon. ﴿A place﴾ i.e., a spot. ﴿That enrages the disbelievers﴾ i.e., their treading angers them. ﴿Nor do they gain any gain from an enemy﴾ such as killing, capture, or plunder. ﴿But a righteous deed is written for them thereby﴾ i.e., they merit reward by it, and that is among the things that make accompanying him obligatory. ﴿Indeed God does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾ for their good deeds. This is a justification for ﴿is written﴾ and an alert that jihad is an act of goodness. As regards the disbelievers, it is because he strives to perfect them to the utmost extent possible, like the physician who strikes the madman. As regards the believers, it is because it is a safeguard for them against the violence and domination of the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 121:

﴿And they spend no small expenditure﴾ even if it is a single cord (ʿallāqah). ﴿Nor a large one﴾ like what ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) spent in the army of hardship (jaysh al-ʿusrah). ﴿Nor do they cross a valley﴾ in their journey, and it is every winding course through which the torrent passes; it is an active participle from wadiya, meaning it flowed, and it became common to denote the land. ﴿Except that it is written for them﴾ it is recorded for them that. ﴿That Allah may reward them﴾ thereby. ﴿For the best of what they used to do﴾ as a reward for the best of their deeds, or the best reward for their deeds.(p-102)

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 122:**

﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together.﴾ It is not proper for them to go forth all together for a campaign (ghazw) or for seeking knowledge ('ilm), just as it is not proper for them all to hold back, for that would disrupt the affairs of livelihood (ma'ash). ﴿Why then should not a group from every division of them go forth?﴾ Why should not a small group go forth from every large community, such as a tribe or the people of a town? ﴿That they may gain understanding (yatafaqqahu) in the religion﴾ That they may exert themselves to acquire fiqh (understanding, jurisprudence) in it and endure the hardships of obtaining it. ﴿And that they may warn their people when they return to them﴾ And that they may make the goal of their striving and the main purpose of their fiqh the guidance and warning of the people. Its mention specifically is because it is more important. In it is evidence that fiqh and admonition (tadhkir) are collective obligations (fard al-kifaya), and that the aim of the student of knowledge in it should be to become upright and to set others upright, not to seek superiority over people or to spread himself throughout the lands. ﴿So that they may beware﴾ meaning, in the hope that they may beware of what they are warned against. It has been cited as evidence that solitary reports (akhbar al-ahad) are authoritative (hujjah), because the generality of "every group" requires that from every three who settle in a village, a group should go forth to acquire fiqh so as to warn their group, that they may take heed and beware. If reports were not accepted unless they reached the level of mass transmission (tawatur), this would not serve any purpose. I have thoroughly discussed this matter, both affirming and objecting, in my book "al-Mirsad". It has been said that the verse has another meaning: when what was revealed about those who stayed behind was revealed, the believers rushed to go forth and ceased seeking fiqh. So they were commanded that from every group a party should go forth to jihad, while their remaining descendants continue to seek fiqh, so that the fiqh which is the greater jihad does not cease, because disputation by proof is the foundation and the chief purpose of the mission. Accordingly, the pronoun in "liyatafaqqahu" and "liyundhiru" refers to the remaining groups after the parties that went forth for the campaign, and the pronoun in "raja'u" refers to the parties, meaning: and that the remaining ones may warn their people, the ones who went forth, when they return to them with the knowledge they gained during their absence.

O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers. They were commanded to fight the nearest of them, then the next nearest, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was first commanded to warn his closest kinsmen, since the nearer is more deserving of compassion and of reform. And it has been said: they are the Jews around Madinah, such as Qurayzah, al-Nadir and Khaybar. And it has been said: they are the Romans, for they were dwelling in al-Sham, which is close to Madinah.

﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾: severity and steadfastness in fighting. It is recited with a fatha and with a damma on the ghayn (ghilzah / ghulzah), and both are two dialects for it.

﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾: by protection and help.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 124–125:

﴿And when a surah is sent down, among them are some who say﴾ — from among the hypocrites — ﴿"Which of you has had its faith increased by this?"﴾ — in denial and mockery. ﴿"Which of you has had its faith increased by this surah?"﴾ — ﴿"Which of you"﴾ is also read as ﴿"Which of you"﴾ in the accusative (ayyakum), by supposing a verb implied, which is explained by ﴿has had it increased﴾.

﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith﴾ — through the increase in knowledge gained from reflecting upon the surah, and the joining of faith in it and in what it contains to their existing faith. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ at its descent, because it is a cause of the increase of their perfection and the elevation of their ranks.

﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ — that is, disbelief — ﴿it has added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾ — disbelief in it, joined to their disbelief in other things. ﴿And they die while they are disbelievers﴾ — and that became firmly established in them until they died upon it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 126–127:

(p-103)﴿Do they not see﴾, meaning the hypocrites. It is also read with the letter tā' (﴿Do you not see﴾). ﴿that they are tested﴾, i.e., afflicted with various kinds of calamities, or through fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they witness the signs that manifest through him. ﴿once or twice every year, then they do not repent﴾, i.e., they do not desist, nor do they repent of their hypocrisy. ﴿Nor do they take heed﴾, i.e., nor do they learn a lesson.

﴿And when a surah is sent down, some of them look at others﴾, they exchange winks with their eyes, in denial of it and in mockery, or out of rage at what it contains of their faults. ﴿Does anyone see you?﴾, i.e., they say: "Does anyone see you if you rise from the presence of the Messenger (ﷺ)?" If no one sees them, they get up; and if someone sees them, they remain seated. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ from his presence, for fear of disgrace. ﴿Allah has turned their hearts﴾ away from faith, and this may be understood as a report or as a supplication. ﴿because they﴾, by reason of the fact that they are ﴿a people who do not understand﴾, due to their poor comprehension or their failure to reflect.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 128–129:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves.﴾ From your own kind, an Arab like you. It is also read "min anfasikum" (from your most noble ones), meaning: from the most noble of you.

﴿It grieves him greatly﴾ it is severe and burdensome to him. ﴿that you suffer hardship﴾ your distress and your encountering of what is disliked. ﴿He is ardently concerned for you﴾ meaning for your faith and the betterment of your condition. ﴿For the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ whether among you or among others. ﴿Kind and merciful﴾ he mentioned the more intensive of the two, which is "ra'uf," because ra'fah is an intense form of mercy, in observance of the rhyme (fawasil).

﴿But if they turn away﴾ from faith in you. ﴿Say: "Allah is sufficient for me"﴾ for He suffices you against their harm and helps you against them. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ as a proof of this. ﴿In Him I have put my trust﴾ so I hope in none and fear none except Him. ﴿He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾ the Mighty King, or the Mighty Body that encompasses all, from which the decrees and the destinies descend. It is also read "al-'azimu" in the nominative (raf'), as an adjective of Lord. It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, that the last of what was revealed were these two verses. And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The Qur'an was revealed to me only verse by verse and letter by letter, except Surah Bara'ah and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad, for these two were revealed to me, and with them were seventy thousand rows of angels." And Allah knows best.
